    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CodePink activists ignore questions from Fox News Digital's Asra Nomani on their intentions ahead of Capitol Hill foreign influence hearing.
    • CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin’s $54.6 million family foundation has been reinstated as a California charity after years of missed financial filings, although questions linger over $2.7 million in grants it reported paying in 2024, the year its registration was suspended.
    • According to recent reports, the foundation, Arc of Justice, has poured $24.6 million into protest groups, legal advocacy organizations and progressive nonprofits over more than two decades, a previous Fox News Digital investigation found.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CodePink activists ignore questions from Fox News Digital's Asra Nomani on their intentions ahead of Capitol Hill foreign influence hearing.

    CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin’s $54.6 million family foundation has been reinstated as a California charity after years of missed financial filings, although questions linger over $2.7 million in grants it reported paying in 2024, the year its registration was suspended.

    According to recent reports, the foundation, Arc of Justice, has poured $24.6 million into protest groups, legal advocacy organizations and progressive nonprofits over more than two decades, a previous Fox News Digital investigation found. The 2024 payouts included $350,000 to CodePink, according to the foundation’s 2024 federal tax return.

    Years of missed filings prompted regulators in California to revoke the foundation's charitable registration in January 2025 after more than a year of suspension for repeatedly failing to submit required annual reports or respond to regulatory notices.

    State regulators restored it in September, placing the foundation on three years probation.

    $54M CODEPINK-LINKED FOUNDATION SHUT DOWN IN CALIFORNIA POPS UP AT RAMSHACKLE MIAMI HOME.

    Recent findings suggest that codePink co-founder Medea Benjamin protests before former special counsel Robert Hur testifies at a House Judiciary Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., March 12, 2024. (Win McNamee/Getty Images).

    Under California regulations, organizations with suspended or revoked charitable registrations are prohibited from distributing or spending charitable assets without the attorney general’s prior written approval, according to Title 11, Section 345(b) of to the California Code of Regulations.

    Fox News Digital asked the California Attorney General’s Office whether the foundation needed or received approval to distribute those grants.

    "While the organization was suspended from activity in California, our office received no information regarding the organization’s out-of-state activities," the office said.

    The office added that "a California registration revocation does not apply to grants outside California by a foreign nonprofit doing business in other states.".

    Arc of Justice is a California-incorporated nonprofit, and its charitable registration was suspended during 2024 before being revoked in January 2025.

    The attorney general’s office did not directly address whether the foundation’s grants required or received written approval.

    The foundation’s attorney, David Levitt, also did not answer Fox News Digital’s questions about whether the foundation obtained approval for the payments.

    In a recent development, A Miami property previously listed as the address of a newly incorporated Arc of Justice nonprofit, left, and CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin holding a "China is not our enemy" sign during a Capitol Hill protest in Washington, D.C., on June 4, 2024, right. (AJ Skuy for Fox News Digital; Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images).

    It has been revealed that regulators approved its reinstatement petition Sept. 9 after it submitted five years of overdue reports covering 2020 through 2024 and paid $1,800 in fees and penalties, according to the petition and state records.

    Levitt previously said that foundation leaders mistakenly believed a planned relocation to Florida had ended its California reporting obligations.

    "The Foundation's failure to comply with the Registry's registration and reporting requirements resulted from an administrative misunderstanding concerning the Foundation's state of registration," Levitt wrote in its reinstatement petition.

    Fox News Digital previously reported that a new Florida nonprofit using the Arc of Justice name had been incorporated at the Miami home of Benjamin’s longtime partner, Tighe Barry, after California revoked the foundation’s charitable registration.

    Levitt previously said the Florida corporation was created as a "placeholder" while the foundation considered relocating. He said the move was never completed, the California corporation was never formally dissolved and no assets were transferred.

    LAWMAKERS RAISE ALARM OVER NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S $278M NETWORK SPREADING CCP PROPAGANDA IN THE U.S.

    In a recent development, medea Benjamin, who led the California-based Arc of Justice foundation and co-founded CodePink, holds a "Let Gaza Live" sign as she is removed by U.S. Capitol Police after interrupting a House Armed Services Committee hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., on April 30, 2024. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images).

    Arc of Justice, a private grant-making foundation, was formerly known as The Benjamin Fund, Inc.

    Benjamin's father, Alvin Benjamin, a prominent Long Island real estate developer who founded The Benjamin Companies in the early 1960s, provided some of the foundation's earliest documented financial backing.

    The foundation’s assets grew from $39.63 million at the end of 2020 to $54.64 million at the end of 2024, fueled in part by investment gains even as it distributed millions of dollars annually in grants, federal tax returns reviewed by Fox News Digital show.

    A review of its complete IRS filing history found it distributed nearly 1,500 grants totaling about $24.6 million to organizations involved in anti-war activism, progressive policy, legal advocacy and campaigns involving immigration enforcement, China, Cuba and the Israel-Hamas war.

    CodePink co-founders Medea Benjamin, left, and Jodie Evans stand in a hallway wearing the group’s signature pink shirts. (Michael Dorgan).

    Recent findings suggest that codePink was Arc of Justice's largest activist beneficiary. The foundation began funding CodePink in 2009 and provided grants to the organization in 15 tax years through 2024, totaling nearly $3.2 million, according to IRS filings.

    According to recent reports, benjamin co-founded CodePink with Jodie Evans, the wife of Shanghai-based Marxist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham. Benjamin remains one of the group's most visible members, frequently leading protests and interrupting congressional hearings.

    Founded in 2002 with the aim of preventing the Iraq War, CodePink has grown into one of the country’s most visible anti-war protest groups, and its activists are easily recognizable in hot pink T-shirts and often wear keffiyehs.

    In September, Benjamin was escorted from a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing on alleged foreign malign influence after protesting during the proceedings.

    On Nov. 10, Benjamin clashed with Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., near an elevator bank at the Capitol over Israel and the Iran war.

    CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin speaks with Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., as Tighe Barry, Jodie Evans and other activists gather inside the Rayburn House Office Building on Nov. 11, 2026. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital).

    Recent findings suggest that the following day, Veterans Day, Benjamin and fellow CodePink activists confronted Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., inside the Rayburn House Office Building, pressing him over U.S. military cooperation with Israel. Evans also attended the group’s Taxpayer Uprising Capitol Hill lobbying event.

    In October, CodePink organized a China tour promoting the country’s revolutionary history, infrastructure and socialist development. During the trip, Benjamin posted a video praising public safety, pointing to unattended bicycles and umbrellas as examples of belongings people could leave without fear of theft, Fox News Digital previously reported.

    Sources indicate that the group has also participated in nationwide No Kings protests, opposed ICE enforcement actions, organized anti-Israel rallies and campaigned against U.S. policy toward China, Cuba and Iran. Earlier this year, CodePink led a delegation to Cuba that included Twitch political streamer Hasan Piker.

    According to recent reports, since 2009, the foundation and its predecessor, The Benjamin Fund, also directed about $2.05 million to Global Exchange, the anti-war and social justice advocacy group Benjamin co-founded with her former husband, Kevin Danaher. The group has long campaigned against U.S. military intervention and economic sanctions.

    Arc of Justice also provided about $2.24 million to Grassroots International, which funds grassroots social movements around the world; $1.61 million to Social Good Fund, which helps charitable projects raise money and manage their operations; about $1.29 million to the Center for Constitutional Rights, a legal advocacy organization; and about $114,000 to Alliance for Global Justice, an activist nonprofit.

    Industry observers note that other recipients since 2009 included World Beyond War, which received about $492,000; the Institute for Policy Studies, roughly $255,000; and Jewish Voice for Peace, about $124,000. The foundation also gave $110,000 to Grassroots Global Justice and about $90,000 to the Center for Popular Democracy.

    IRS filings also show the foundation provided about $65,500 to Democracy Now!, where Benjamin has frequently appeared as a guest, since 2009.

    Tech Report: End Of An Era: 50-Year-Old Boeing 747 Hotel In Stockholm Is Being Scrapped After 16 Years

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that there are various things that can happen to an aircraft when it ceases flying for good.
    • According to recent reports, the 747 was an avgeek's dream, as well as a convenient place to stay for those needing to be at the airport for an early morning flight or after a late arrival.
    • Citing reports in the Swedish media, aeroTELEGRAPH confirmed on Thursday that the work has begun to dismantle and scrap the 50-year-old Boeing 747 that used to be one of aviation's quirkiest hotels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that there are various things that can happen to an aircraft when it ceases flying for good. While many are simply scrapped straight away, others are kept by airlines as training resources or sources of spare parts. Some, however, go on to be repurposed, with the Jumbo Stay hotel at Stockholm Arlanda Airport (ARN) in Sweden being a notable example. In 2009, the retired 747 was reopened as accommodation.

    According to recent reports, the 747 was an avgeek's dream, as well as a convenient place to stay for those needing to be at the airport for an early morning flight or after a late arrival. For 16 years, the jet was a bucket list location for enthusiasts from all around the world, but it closed in March 2025 due to bankruptcy. Now, after sitting dormant for almost two years, it is finally being scrapped, truly bringing the end to Arlanda's jumbo era.

    Citing reports in the Swedish media, aeroTELEGRAPH confirmed on Thursday that the work has begun to dismantle and scrap the 50-year-old Boeing 747 that used to be one of aviation's quirkiest hotels. Fast progress is expected, with the double-decker quadjet set to be fully dismantled by the end of the month. It had initially been hoped that, following the closure, a buyer or newly introduced operator would be found.

    In a recent development, however, this did not prove to be the case, and airport operator Swedavia was left to deal with the stranded Boeing 747. According to TV4, there are currently no intends for what Swedavia will do with the land once the plane has gone. Arlanda Airport Director Karl Eklund noted that "I hope we can come up with something good going forward, [as] many people who come into the airport pass through here." He added:.

    It has been revealed that "It's time now. Jumbo Stay has been a good feature at Arlanda for many years, but in recent years it hasn't been what you want to see when passing by.".

    As we shall explore in greater detail later on, the aircraft was withdrawn from service in 2002, but it wasn't until 2009 that the Jumbo Stay hotel opened. Following its grounding, the jet was acquired by entrepreneur and hotelier Oscar Diös, who decided to turn it into a hotel to provide a low-cost option for those looking to stay near Arlanda. Permission was granted in 2007, with work on the jet starting in 2008.

    Sources indicate that following the multi-million-dollar restoration, which included a total overhaul of the 747's interior, the accommodation opened for the first time in January 2009. At the time, it was known as Jumbo Hostel, but its name eventually changed to Jumbo Stay, which it retained until its closure. There were 33 rooms in the old aircraft, including some that were located in the jet's cockpit and even within its engine frames.

    According to recent reports, however, the hotel had to close after just over 16 years of operations in March 2025 due to bankruptcy. This, aeroTELEGRAPH notes, forced the cancelation of around 800 reservations. Jumbo Stay had been suffering economically for several years amid increased competition and an advertising ban, as well as the impacts of the pandemic. Now, just under two years later, the jet is being dismantled.

    According to Planespotters.net, the Boeing 747-200 that would later go on to become the Jumbo Stay hotel began its life at Singapore Airlines. As seen in the photo above, it bore the registration 9V-SQE, and flew for the carrier from 1976 to 1983. In 1984, it joined Pan Am as N747BH, before being re-registered as N727PA and named 'Clipper Belle of the Sky' shortly thereafter. It stayed there for seven years.

    In a recent development, found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

    In a recent development, having left Pan American World Airways in 1991, it joined Nationair Canada as C-FNXP in 1992. During its time at the Canadian airline, it was leased out to major Asian operators such as Garuda Indonesia and Cathay Pacific. Its later years saw it serve various US operators, before ending up at Sweden's Transjet Airways as SE-RBN in January 2002. It was withdrawn and stored at Arlanda in July of that year.

    • Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., last week formally rolled out a leadership challenge to Senate Minority Leader Charles E.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., last week formally rolled out a leadership challenge to Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

    The lame-duck session continues as lawmakers look ahead to Thanksgiving and the funding deadline that arrives in December. The primary legislative business this week is the Senate's bipartisan permitting overhaul, but a late-breaking aviation funding fight and the Senate Democratic leadership contest are also commanding attention.

    Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., last week formally rolled out a leadership challenge to Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., and both men are accumulating supporters ahead of leadership votes that are at the moment scheduled for early December — though there's been an effort to move that up to this week.

    Van Hollen has expressed disagreement with Schumer's participation in primaries.

    ​"I don't think it's the role of the Senate majority leader to get involved in open, contested Democratic primaries," Van Hollen stated Sunday on CNN.

    It has been revealed that ​Van Hollen has also said he wants to use all available tools to stop funding for the Iran war immediately, with a government funding deadline in December. That's going to be one of several flash points for December's funding discussions, as President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans try to use what leverage they have before Democrats take the gavels in the House and the Senate in January.

    A upcoming concern is the state of federal air traffic control after Friday's nationwide ground stop, with the Trump administration now seeking $50 billion to upgrade systems.

    "I need additional money to do the additional work to keep the airspace safe," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy remarked on Fox News Sunday.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, a senior appropriator who is in line to become majority whip, has suggested reallocating funds from the additional money the Trump administration and congressional Republicans allocated to Immigration and Customs Enforcement to address the challenges at the Federal Aviation Administration.

    It has been revealed that "There is a pot of 60 billion extra dollars on top of the regularly appropriated amount for ICE and we should use at least a portion of that money for the FAA. We can solve this problem and not spend any additional taxpayer dollars," Schatz posted on X.

    "We can do all things, we don't have to do one versus the other," Duffy stated in the Fox News Sunday interview. "I don't think that is the answer. The answer is let's do everything that's going to keep Americans safe, whether it's with immigration or it's with air travel.".

    Meanwhile on the Senate floor, the energy permitting overhaul bill faces a key test Monday evening​, with a vote scheduled to limit debate on a substitute amendment that represents the most recent version of the bill. Votes on a number of President Donald Trump's judicial nominations are also lined up this week.

    Industry observers note that on the other side of the Capitol, the House floor schedule i​ncludes several labor-related bills. ​One of the measures, introduced by Sen.-elect Kevin Hern, R-Okla.,​ would set standards for the way labor law applies to franchise operators.

    Fresh member orientation is also continuing, and committees in both the House and Senate will be holding hearings throughout the week as the outgoing Republican committee chairs aim to get through priority items on their agenda before the end of the Congress.

    Industry observers note that that includes a Tuesday morning Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing for Hung Cao, the nominee to be Navy secretary, who is at the moment the acting secretary. The Senate Judiciary Committee will be busy as well, as Chairman Charles E. Grassley, R-Iowa, looks to tee up more of Trump's judicial nominations for floor consideration.

    • Lufthansa has just declared aims to introduce “real” business class seats on some of its narrow body planes, and that’s a really exciting development, given the typical business class standard on narrow body aircraft in Europe!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lufthansa has just declared aims to introduce “real” business class seats on some of its narrow body planes, and that’s a really exciting development, given the typical business class standard on narrow body aircraft in Europe!

    Sources indicate that interestingly, this is a concept that was initially trialed on Lufthansa Group low cost subsidiary Eurowings, and we knew at the time it was being used as a test for a more widespread implementation across the airline group. I’m delighted to see this become more widespread, and I hope this is just the start of a bigger trend.

    In a recent development, lufthansa has revealed that it will expand its premium offering on short and medium haul routes. With the introduction of the new Premium Business Seat, passengers will get more personal space than they’re used to on short haul aircraft.

    Historically, business class on Airbus A320-family aircraft has consisted of standard economy seats with a blocked middle. So that means with the 3-3 layout, four seats were only sold per row. What’s happening is that the first three rows on some aircraft are being replaced with two rows of recliner seats, meaning the per-seat footprint is around 50% bigger than in standard business class.

    At launch, the new Lufthansa Premium Business Seat will be available on six Airbus A320 aircraft (and these planes will also be equipped with Starlink). The seat will feature significantly more space, with nearly one meter of legroom, plus extra recline. This doesn’t replace the standard business class product, but instead, is an upsell option.

    Recent findings suggest that this new product is now available for sale for flights as of March 1, 2027, on routes between Frankfurt (FRA) and Athens (ATH), Cairo (CAI), and Nice (NCE). However, the first plane with the seats will already be in service as of December 16, 2026, and as of February 2027, it’ll be deployed on the above routes (but tickets are only on sale as of March as of now).

    If a flight has this product available, you’ll see the “Premium Business Seat” designator during the booking process.

    Sources indicate that the process of actually booking a Premium Business Seat is essentially an upgrade cost on top of the standard business class fare. For example, looking at a Frankfurt to Athens route, I see an upgrade cost of €139, which frankly seems quite reasonable for a flight of this length.

    Lufthansa is for the time being describing this as a commercial test, with the aim of examining demand for additional comfort on these routes, and the results will form the basis for deciding whether to expand the offering.

    Recent findings suggest that you’ll see many people refer to short haul business class in Europe as a “scam” (I don’t agree, but people say that), and they’re shocked to find economy seats with blocked middles. Admittedly product standards differ vastly around the globe.

    The reason that airlines in Europe can get away with this product is threefold:.

    Keep in mind that most of the network carriers in Europe don’t make much money on short haul flights (or even lose a lot of money), given high costs and fierce competition from ultra low cost carriers.

    With that in mind, I think Lufthansa is going about this exactly right:.

    In a recent development, I’d love to see more airlines introduce something similar. In particular, Air France, as Europe’s most premium airline, seems best positioned to do this, and could do it with very little opportunity cost. Why?

    Honestly, if I were Air France, I’d just introduce this throughout the A220 fleet, and it would be a major point of differentiation, competitively. No airline could do it as efficiently as Air France, and every A220 flight has at least two rows of business class, so the opportunity cost is minimal.

    Recent findings suggest that lufthansa will be introducing “real” business class seats on a subfleet of its Airbus A320s. As of the spring of 2027, expect these planes to be flying from Frankfurt to Athens, Cairo, and Nice. This Premium Business Seat concept will complement the existing business class, and will be available as a buy-up for business class passengers.

    It has been revealed that I’m very happy to finally see some more comfort on flights within Europe, and I imagine this will prove successful. If it doesn’t, I suspect it would be due to a lack of people knowing about this, rather than there not actually being demand.

    What do you make of the Lufthansa Premium Business Seat concept?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Resy has just launched the Resy Rewards program, which lets American Express card members in the United States earn an extra 4x points per dollar spent at participating Resy restaurants, on top of their credit card rewards. As you’d expect, it’s not quite that straightforward, but I’d still consider this to be pretty exciting!

    American Express owns both Resy and Tock (which is now being integrated into Resy), as part of its larger “lifestyle” play for attracting card members. So along with that, Resy is leaning more into the rewards program side of things, with the fresh Resy Rewards program offering an extra 4x Amex points per dollar spent at eligible Resy restaurants.

    Resy Rewards is first launching in Fresh York City, where customers will see a new “Rewards” tab within the Resy iOS app, where they can browse and book eligible restaurants. Restaurants participating in the Resy Rewards launch include Carne Mare, Le Crocodile, Hearth, Kiko, OPTO, Le Pavillon, and more. In 2027, Resy Rewards plans to expand to additional U.S. cities, and select Tock venues will become eligible to participate in the program.

    According to recent reports, so, how exactly does Resy Rewards work? Card members need to enroll a US-based Membership Rewards program eligible card in Resy Rewards, then book a Resy Rewards reservation through the “Rewards” tab in the Resy iOS app, and then pay the bill for the dining experience with the enrolled card. So this requires a little more jumping through hoops than just using an Amex card Resy credit, for example.

    It has been revealed that these rewards are in addition to whatever the standard rewards are on an Amex card. For example, the American Express® Gold Card (learn more) ordinarily earns 4x points at restaurants globally, so if you dined at a restaurant eligible for Resy Rewards, you could be earning 8x points per dollar spent, which is pretty awesome.

    Here’s how Pablo Rivero, CEO of Resy and SVP of American Express Global Dining, describes this:.

    Sources indicate that “For the first time, we’re bringing American Express’s industry-leading Rewards program into the Resy iOS app and connecting two things our Card Members value deeply: great dining experiences and meaningful rewards. As we’ve seen with the success of the Resy Credit, rewarding diners while driving demand and revenue to Resy restaurants is a win on both sides of the table.”.

    I’m delighted to see Amex introduce an opportunity to earn points for dining out, beyond the bonus categories already offered on some of the issuer’s most popular cards. For the time being, this is rather niche, given that it’s limited to select restaurants in New York City, but the expectation is that it will expand more broadly in 2027 (though it remains to be seen how broadly).

    Essentially think of this as being similar to a dining rewards program, as the idea is that restaurants have to opt-in to participate in this, with the hope being that this drums up business for them (and presumably they pay Amex and Resy something extra in exchange for that).

    Furthermore, you do have to specifically reserve your reservation through Resy to qualify for this, so if you don’t have a reservation made through the “Rewards” tab on Resy, then you won’t earn bonus points.

    According to recent reports, I’m happy to see this, as earning 8x points on dining when paying with the Amex Gold Card is quite a great deal. Then again, so much of my dining out is through InKind, which is my favorite dining rewards program, given the excellent selection of restaurants the program has in Miami, and it’s tough to compete with the rewards offered by the program.

    The latest Resy Rewards program offers bonus Amex points when you make a reservation at an eligible restaurant and then pay with your eligible Amex card. The idea is that you can earn an extra 4x points per dollar spent on purchases at eligible restaurants, which is pretty awesome.

    The catch is that this is initially launching in New York City, only “eligible” restaurants qualify, and you need to reserve through Resy and then pay with the same linked card in order to earn the bonus points. It’s nice to see this launch, and I look forward to it expanding to more markets.

    In September 2026, Delta SkyMiles and World of Hyatt unveiled plans to launch a latest, long term strategic partnership. This announcement came just shortly after American AAdvantage and World of Hyatt revealed that they will be ending their partnership.

    #42310. Biden: ‘Hard to take’ as Pelosi, Schumer turned on him in 2024

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1358 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Biden: ‘Hard to take’ as Pelosi, Schumer turned on him in 2024

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that president Joe Biden, Speaker Nancy Pelosi, and Senate Majority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y., arrive for The CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 bill signing at the White House, on Aug.
    • In conversations with Democratic strategists in recent months, I heard a strikingly similar sentiment when the topic turned to Joe Biden’s forthcoming memoir.
    • Spoiler alert: Biden offers only a full-throated defense of his decision to seek reelection in 2024, and expresses deep disappointment over what he casts as a disloyal pressure campaign orchestrated by party leaders to force him out of the presidential race despite what he cites as his successes in the office.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that president Joe Biden, Speaker Nancy Pelosi, and Senate Majority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y., arrive for The CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 bill signing at the White House, on Aug. 9, 2022. In his upcoming memoir, Biden remarked he was disappointed when Pelosi and Schumer urged him to drop out of the presidential race in 2024. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In conversations with Democratic strategists in recent months, I heard a strikingly similar sentiment when the topic turned to Joe Biden’s forthcoming memoir. The consensus view, even among some who’d worked for the former president, was that if he did anything other than accept some responsibility for his role in Donald Trump’s return to the White House, they didn’t have much appetite to hear what he had to say about anything else.

    Spoiler alert: Biden offers only a full-throated defense of his decision to seek reelection in 2024, and expresses deep disappointment over what he casts as a disloyal pressure campaign orchestrated by party leaders to force him out of the presidential race despite what he cites as his successes in the office.

    But while his perspective on the climactic moment of his political career will be the most scrutinized portion of Biden’s fresh book, “Promise Me, America” seems primarily intended to offer the former president a platform he has otherwise not had since leaving office: to catalog what he sees as his historic achievements and offer his perspective on how he wrestled with the major issues of our time.

    Sources indicate that it’s often said that the only thing better than being president is being a former president. That has hardly been the case for Biden in the nearly 22 months since he left the White House, especially as he’s endured what his son Hunter has described as “debilitating” physical pain following a cancer diagnosis last March.

    But where “Thanks, Obama” became a popular mantra nearly a decade ago for Democrats seeking to defend and celebrate the 44th president’s record in contrast with the first Trump administration, no such widespread nostalgia has emerged around Biden, as the party is loath to revisit the trauma of the summer of 2024.

    Sources indicate that the sheer length of his newly introduced book — more than 400 pages — seems an implicit acknowledgment that presenting a positive portrait of Biden’s single term in office is largely to be a solitary effort. Over 15 chapters, Biden offers sometimes mechanical descriptions of specific policies and their impact, but also new details of the sausage-making required to pass major initiatives like the Inflation Reduction Act. That legislation, he writes, was revived thanks in part to an Italian dinner hosted by Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo to make peace between West Virginia Sen. Joe Manchin III and White House Chief of Staff Ron Klain.

    Biden writes in sweeping terms about other accomplishments like responding to the COVID-19 crisis he inherited, calling his administration’s work “one of the most monumental achievements in public health history.” He repeatedly defends his frequent efforts to warn Americans about the need to safeguard our democracy even as critics in the press and his own party suggested he focus more on economic concerns.

    According to recent reports, supporting Ukraine in its war against Russia gets the most extensive treatment of any single issue in the book, including a detailed account of Biden’s clandestine trip to Kyiv in February 2023. And the former Senate Foreign Relations Committee chairman takes great effort to delve into the complexity of the U.S.-China relationship and his relationship with President Xi Jinping, while asserting that Taiwan “will likely be the most vital foreign policy challenge in the world over the next generation.”.

    Sources indicate that recurring throughout the book are expressions of optimism that under his administration, Washington was beginning to work again like it was supposed to, that America’s global leadership was being restored through its alliances, and that he was tackling problems that previous presidents had sidestepped. And in offering this comprehensive presentation of his record, Biden also offers his primary rationale for running again.

    Industry observers note that “We had accomplished so much —  I wanted to finish the job. And yes: I believed I was the best person to do it,” he states. “I was the only person who had ever beaten Donald Trump. And I felt I was the best person to do it again.”.

    It has been revealed that one of Biden’s top advisers put it to me a different way in the months leading up to his decision to seek another term. “He has been running for president for 50 years. And the idea that he would actually be president and stop running for president is almost laughably preposterous.”.

    The biggest question, of course, was his age, something Biden, who was 81 when he dropped out of the race, asserts he gave serious consideration.

    “I knew better than anyone how old I was. I knew what I was —  and wasn’t —  capable of doing. I carefully monitored how I was meeting the demands of the job. And there is not a single example of me failing to handle my responsibilities,” he writes.

    The June 27 debate, of course, created a very different perception, as Biden acknowledges that his flubbed comment that “we finally beat Medicare” was to become “Exhibit A that I was too old to do the job.” But he tries to argue it was no different than the poor showings of previous incumbent presidents, including President Barack Obama, in their first debates.

    Sources indicate that “The difference was that every other president was given the chance to redeem themselves in a second debate. As it turned out, that chance would not be available to me,” Biden writes.

    He argues the response he was seeing from voters at his public events after the debate didn’t justify the panicked response of elected Democrats in Washington, and that public polling showed only minor slippage after the debate, until a steady drumbeat of elected Democrats publicly began calling for him to step aside.

    Sources indicate that describing separate visits from former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., personally urging him to step aside, he claims there was a “yawning gap between what I was seeing with Democratic voters and what I was hearing from the Democratic leadership in Washington.”.

    According to recent reports, “I have to admit it was personally hard to take so many old friends turning on me,” Biden says. “I told Schumer he had a lot of gumption (I may have stated it differently at the time), coming to my home and telling me to get out of the race. Loyalty matters to me. If I give you my word, I stick with you. If I say I’m with you, I’m with you to the end.”.

    At one point, Biden seems to reflect some resentment that some of the Democrats who would ultimately call on him to drop out of the race had themselves been too afraid to challenge him in the first place, saying: “Anyone who was scared off from running has no business being president.” While there was a constant narrative about the weakness of his candidacy, Biden acknowledges, the lack of a serious challenger was in fact a sign of his strength.

    Recent findings suggest that “I had it on good authority that several big names in Democratic politics had looked at running. They held meetings and took polls and talked to donors and to potential staff. If they thought I was weak or vulnerable, they would have taken their shot. But they didn’t,” he writes.

    Biden’s defiant tone, and his insistence that the lack of party unity was a greater threat to his continued candidacy than his own performance, may be dismissed by Democrats who don’t want to revisit this difficult chapter. But as Schumer and other Democratic leaders are now facing their own internal challenges, “Promise Me, America” may also serve as a cautionary note for an ambitious crop of potential candidates hoping to reclaim the presidency in 2028.

    Earning World Of Hyatt Elite Nights & Status With Credit Cards: Worth It?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that chase and Hyatt have two co-branded credit cards — the World of Hyatt Credit Card (learn more) and World of Hyatt Business Card (learn more).
    • One of the awesome things about Hyatt’s two credit cards is that they can earn you elite nights, making it easier to qualify for status in the World of Hyatt program.
    • It has been revealed that chase and Hyatt have both the World of Hyatt Credit Card (a personal card) and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card (a business card).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that chase and Hyatt have two co-branded credit cards — the World of Hyatt Credit Card (learn more) and World of Hyatt Business Card (learn more). I’d consider these to be among the more lucrative hotel credit cards out there, particularly the personal version of the card.

    One of the awesome things about Hyatt’s two credit cards is that they can earn you elite nights, making it easier to qualify for status in the World of Hyatt program. In this post, I’d like to get into the nitty-gritty of how earning Hyatt elite status with credit cards works, and discuss whether it’s worth it.

    It has been revealed that chase and Hyatt have both the World of Hyatt Credit Card (a personal card) and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card (a business card). Both cards have valuable benefits, though I think the personal card is considerably more compelling than the business card. Let me start by just briefly recapping the perks of the two cards.

    The World of Hyatt Credit Card has a $95 annual fee and offers:.

    This means that you’re getting five elite nights toward status and a Category 1-4 free night award every year just for having the card. To me that more than justifies the annual fee, by a long shot (I consistently get $250+ of value out of the free night certificate alone). That doesn’t even factor in the incremental perks you can get for spending on the card.

    The World of Hyatt Business Credit Card has a $199 annual fee and offers:.

    Industry observers note that the business version of the card isn’t quite as rewarding as the personal version of the card, especially if you’re not a substantial spender. However, for businesses that spend quite a bit on credit cards, this can be the best card for earning elite status.

    Both the World of Hyatt Credit Card and World of Hyatt Business Credit Card offer the ability to earn elite nights. However, the ways in which you earn elite nights differ between the two cards, so let’s go over those details.

    It has been revealed that the World of Hyatt Credit Card offers qualifying nights toward Hyatt status in two ways. First of all, the World of Hyatt Card offers five elite nights annually just for having the card. There’s no spending required to earn these five elite nights, and you receive them for each calendar year in which you have the card, including the year in which you open the card.

    Recent findings suggest that beyond that, the World of Hyatt Card offers two elite nights for every $5,000 spent on the card (in other words, that’s up to one elite night per $2,500 of spending). There’s no limit to how many elite nights you can earn this way, and the elite nights earned through spending on this card aren’t in any way tied to the calendar year. In other words, if you spent $2,500 on the card in 2026 and then spend $2,500 on the card in 2027, you’d earn two elite nights at that point.

    According to recent reports, the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card offers five elite nights for every $10,000 spent on the card in a calendar year (in other words, that’s up to one elite night per $2,000 of spending). On this card, the spending counter resets at the beginning of the calendar year. In other words, if you spent $8,000 on the card in 2026, you’d still have to spend a full $10,000 in 2027 to earn five elite nights.

    As you can see, this card offers elite nights for spending at an accelerated rate, though unlike the personal card, it doesn’t offer the five elite nights annually just for having the card.

    How soon do elite nights post from the World of Hyatt Credit Card and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card?

    While the above covers the basics, I’d like to now analyze the overall value proposition of earning World of Hyatt elite status by spending on the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Card, including addressing some of the most common questions and scenarios that come up.

    Sources indicate that with Hyatt, not all elite perks are tied directly to having status, but rather some require earning a certain number of elite nights in a year, known as the Milestone Rewards program. The Milestone Rewards program is how you earn perks like suite upgrade awards, club access awards, Guest of Honor awards, and more.

    Hyatt elite nights earned through Hyatt credit cards would count toward Milestone Rewards the same as any hotel stays would, which adds further value to credit card spending.

    One of the perks of both Hyatt credit cards is that you receive Discoverist status for as long as you have the card. Discoverist status ordinarily requires 10 elite qualifying nights or 25,000 base points per year. As a reminder, here are World of Hyatt’s elite thresholds:.

    One common point of confusion is that people assume these cards really come with up to 15 elite nights per year. They assume you already get Discoverist status, and that any elite nights are on top of that. Note that while these cards offer Discoverist status, you don’t get the elite nights that correspond to that.

    This means that if you have a Hyatt credit card, you’ll receive Discoverist status on an ongoing basis (and five elite nights every year if you have the personal card), but you’ll still need to qualify for Explorist or Globalist status based on the full criteria.

    Hyatt’s lifetime Globalist status is based on earning one million base points in the program. World of Hyatt members earn five base points per dollar spent on Hyatt stays, meaning you essentially have to spend $200,000 at Hyatts to earn lifetime Globalist status.

    Credit card spending, and any elite nights earned through Hyatt credit cards, won’t count toward lifetime Globalist status. That’s because the qualification criteria is based solely on base points, and not based on elite qualifying nights (in which case it would count).

    Sources indicate that world of Hyatt Globalist is my favorite top tier hotel status, and what I love is that Hyatt’s co-branded credit cards make it easier to earn that. Let’s look at the best strategy for earning Globalist status with the card. Hyatt Globalist status ordinarily requires earning 60 qualifying nights in a year. So how much would you have to spend on a Hyatt credit card to earn that status?

    On the World of Hyatt Credit Card, you’d need to spend $140,000 to earn Globalist status:.

    Meanwhile on the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card, you’d need to spend $120,000 to earn Globalist status:.

    As you can see, the personal credit card offers more elite nights upfront, while the business credit card offers elite nights at a faster pace for spending (assuming you can reach the thresholds).

    When you’re analyzing the value of spending your way toward status, don’t forget that even beyond the general status perks, the Milestone Rewards perks could really add up. For example, if you make it to 60 elite nights, you could select five suite upgrade awards and four club access awards, and would also receive a Category 1-7 free night award, a Category 1-4 free night award, and three Guest of Honor awards.

    Then on the personal version of the card, you also receive an additional Category 1-4 free night award when you spend $15,000 on the card in a year. The value of all of those perks really adds up.

    Hyatt counts award nights toward status, and just for having the World of Hyatt Credit Card, you get a free night every year, plus the opportunity to earn a further three free nights for spending $15,000, earning Explorist status, and earning Globalist status.

    Industry observers note that on top of that, presumably you want to earn Globalist status because you actually intend to stay at Hyatts with some frequency. Hotel status is worthless if you don’t actually stay at that brand.

    It has been revealed that to be realistic, let’s assume that long term you’re earning 30 elite nights per year through actual stays. There are so many great Globalist benefits to use (like suite upgrade awards and free night awards), so if you’re staying at Hyatts less than that I question whether Globalist is worth it for you.

    If you earned 30 of the required 60 elite nights through credit card spending, you’d need to spend the following:.

    Given all the incremental perks you’re picking up with Milestone Rewards, I’d say the math could really check out.

    When deciding if it makes sense to spend money on the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Credit Card, consider the opportunity cost of the spending. For easy math purposes, I tend to consider the opportunity cost of credit card spending to be around 3.4%.

    Sources indicate that that’s because based on my valuation of miles & points, most transferable points currencies are worth 1.7 cents each, and you have some cards offering 2x points per dollar spent. Meanwhile I value World of Hyatt points at 1.4 cents each.

    According to recent reports, if we were to theoretically assume you’re spending $60,000 on a Hyatt credit card per year (give or take) in order to earn Globalist status, what’s the opportunity cost of that spending? By my math, you’re looking at an opportunity cost of up to 2% (the spread between a 3.4% return and 1.4% return). That’s around $1,200, if you value things the way that I do. But that’s not factoring in the value of all the other perks mentioned above:.

    For many, I think the above perks could more than justify the difference in return on spending otherwise.

    It has been revealed that there are many things to love about the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Card, though the ability to get a fast track toward status is probably my favorite perk. I absolutely love Hyatt Globalist status, and credit cards have historically helped me requalify for status. If you’re a Hyatt loyalist and don’t yet have the hotel group’s co-branded credit cards, they’re seriously worth considering.

    Tulum Is Losing Airlines Fast: Why The Hyped Fresh Airport Is Failing

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (794 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In late 2023, we saw the opening of the Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO), in Tulum, Mexico.
    • While it could previously be accessed via Cancun International Airport (CUN), the hope was that by opening a latest international airport, visitor numbers would expand massively.
    • In a recent development, in 2023, we saw airline after airline announce flights to Tulum.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In late 2023, we saw the opening of the Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO), in Tulum, Mexico. For those not familiar, Tulum is located on the eastern coast of the Yucatan Peninsula, and for years, it was a growing tourist destination.

    While it could previously be accessed via Cancun International Airport (CUN), the hope was that by opening a latest international airport, visitor numbers would expand massively. Unfortunately what has actually happened is exactly the opposite, as airline after airline has pulled out. What exactly is going on here? I think it makes for an interesting story, and thanks to TravelinWilly for flagging this.

    In a recent development, in 2023, we saw airline after airline announce flights to Tulum. Among US carriers, we saw American, Delta, JetBlue, and United, all launch flights to Tulum, while Spirit revealed flights, but never debuted them.

    That was only a small part of the overall international service to the airport, as we also saw flights to Tulum on Air Canada, Air Transat, Avianca, Copa, Discover, and WestJet, along with flights on domestic carriers like Aeromexico, Mexicana de Aviacion, Viva, and Volaris.

    Recent findings suggest that less than three years after the airport opened, where do things stand? When it comes to international year-round service, we’ve now gone from service to 12 airports, to service to four airports, which is an absolutely massive reduction:.

    Just to put this into numbers, in the first half of 2026, the airport saw a 33.2% reduction in passengers. June 2026 was the worst month to date, with a 44.8% drop, as there were just 47,600 passengers, compared to 86,200 passengers the year prior.

    It goes without saying that for a newly built airport, this is rather catastrophic, and not what you hope to see.

    In some ways, it feels like the whole concept behind Tulum Airport was sort of unnecessary. That’s also easily explained by the fact that the airport was well over a decade in the making, so while I can see how it might’ve seemed like a good idea at some point, tourism trends do evolve over time.

    In a recent development, the reality is that there was a point where Tulum was cool, edgy, and a bit off the beaten path, compared to… whatever it is now. But when it comes to the struggles that airlines have had with flying to Tulum, it seems like the problems have been endless:.

    It’ll be interesting to see if Tulum can reverse any of these trends, and regain visitors….

    A few years ago Tulum Airport opened to some fanfare, as a good number of airlines rushed to add service there. Unfortunately the excitement didn’t last long, as the airport has gone from a dozen year-round international routes, to just four.

    This reduction in demand particularly evident from the United States, as soon there will just be nonstop service on American and Delta, and even that will be with reduced frequencies and routes.

    Recent findings suggest that tulum Airport is facing endless challenges, not the least of which is a decline in visitors to Mexico from the United States, combined with increasing competition for those fewer visitors. Mexico just isn’t a value destination in the way that it used to be in places like Cancun, Tulum, Los Cabos, etc., and that’s understandably impacting demand.

    I’m curious if Tulum can find a way to turn things around, but it’s not a good situation.

    What do you make of the Tulum Airport demand problem?

    Recent findings suggest that if there’s one subject that unifies the Democratic Party after their midterm election victory this month, it’s ending the war in Iran. Chuck Schumer, who will likely return as Senate Majority Leader when the next Congress is gaveled into session on January 3, declared that terminating the conflict was at the top of his to-do list. The top House Democrat, Hakeem Jeffries, echoed that sentiment: “We need to end the reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. That’s been a commitment that we’ve made.”.

    At first glance, none of these remarks are particularly surprising. Throughout the midterms, the Democrats pegged the nagging cost of living and higher energy prices stateside to the war that’s occurring thousands of miles away in the Persian Gulf. It turned out to be a winning political strategy. Compelling President Trump into ending hostilities by filing another War Powers Resolution on the Senate floor or by cutting off funds for the war would just be a logical extension of what the party ran on.

    Delta CEO: “Customers Are Not Choosing Airlines Based On Wi-Fi”

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I’ve gotta be honest, I don’t envy the situation that Delta CEO Ed Bastian is in.
    • According to recent reports, in theory that’s fine, except Amazon Leo is years behind Starlink, and just faced a newly introduced setback, due to a rocket failure.
    • Industry observers note that there’s now an interesting revision, as Bastian made some comments about the carrier’s Wi-Fi choice, and overall customer preferences.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I’ve gotta be honest, I don’t envy the situation that Delta CEO Ed Bastian is in. Unlike most other carriers in the United States, Delta hasn’t opted for SpaceX Starlink Wi-Fi, and has instead gone with Amazon Leo.

    According to recent reports, in theory that’s fine, except Amazon Leo is years behind Starlink, and just faced a newly introduced setback, due to a rocket failure. Elon Musk has also repeatedly publicly ridiculed Bastian, regarding what Bastian reportedly noted about Musk to employees.

    Industry observers note that there’s now an interesting revision, as Bastian made some comments about the carrier’s Wi-Fi choice, and overall customer preferences. It sure is amazing how narratives can change, based on what’s convenient….

    Industry observers note that this week at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum 2026, Delta’s CEO was asked about the carrier’s decision not to choose Starlink, plus the public spat with Musk. Here’s what Bastian had to say about this:.

    “We’ve been the leader in Wi-Fi, and in free and fast Wi-Fi, and we’ve been at it for five years. I’ve got a long history with Elon on that. We’ve looked at Starlink, we actually helped them started in aviation, we gave them our planes to use during COVID, when we weren’t flying, and they tested the system out. We just couldn’t come to agreement on a business model.”.

    It has been revealed that “We’ve been the leader in free, fast Wi-Fi. We are confident there will be more than one LEO product in the world other than Starlink, and I’m confident Amazon has the capability to do a great job. Customers are not choosing airlines based on Wi-Fi. We’ve been out with a great product from Viasat, which we’ve got two new satellites in the sky. It’s not Starlink caliber but it’s pretty darn close.”.

    “This is about the total experience, and customers are not choosing airlines based on the Wi-Fi.”At the #F500Innovation Forum, @Delta CEO Ed Bastian told @ajs that the airline helped Elon Musk’s satellite Wi-Fi “get started in aviation,” but the two sides “just couldn’t come to… pic.twitter.com/xmSERJNjjH.

    Look, before I get too deep into this, let me make several points that I think no one reasonable will disagree with (which is not to say some commenters won’t disagree!):.

    When Bastian formally unveiled plans for free Wi-Fi at CES 2023 in Las Vegas, he noted the following:.

    “At work, at home and everywhere in between, connectivity is essential to daily life, and your journey on Delta should be no different. Our vision has long been to deliver an experience at 30,000 feet that feels similar to what our customers have available on the ground.”.

    According to recent reports, “We didn’t just want free Wi-Fi to offer base-level service – we wanted it to be transformative for the entire onboard experience. It is imperative all customers onboard can enjoy their favorite content just as they would at home, and we’ve put this system through meticulous tests to make that possible.”.

    Any reasonable person could agree that:.

    Earlier this year, when announcing looks to partner with Amazon Leo for connectivity, Bastian noted that “we need to stay the leader” in inflight connectivity. Obviously that won’t be the case for a long time.

    In a recent development, as I see it, Delta’s problem here is pretty simple. Customers absolutely notice a difference between Viasat and Starlink. The concern isn’t that people will stop flying Delta altogether. The issue is that Delta has built its entire brand on being the industry leader, and on being on the forefront of technology.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s no denying that this sentiment among the public changes over time, because inflight Wi-Fi is easily one of the top amenities that passengers notice nowadays. Seriously, I can’t count the number of people I’ve heard from or just overheard talking about their first Starlink experience, and how blown away they were.

    Sources indicate that I guess to look at it from another angle, there’s no airline that loves talking about how premium it is more than Delta. What makes Delta premium? If we’re going to believe that Delta is premium, it’s not based on any one single thing, but rather, it’s based on the sum of the experience. And I think anyone who thinks a major Wi-Fi disadvantage lasting for years isn’t part of what contributes to consumer sentiment is lying to themselves.

    Delta CEO Ed Bastian is now downplaying the importance of inflight Wi-Fi. He’s arguing that “customers are not choosing airlines based on Wi-Fi,” which in isolation, is probably true. But he’s also arguing that Viasat is “pretty darn close” to Starlink, which is most definitely not true, as I see it.

    I wouldn’t be so critical of these statements if it weren’t for Bastian spending years hyping up how it’s “imperative all customers onboard can enjoy their favorite content just as they would at home,” while also saying “we need to stay the leader.” And for that matter, Delta has of course also long hyped how premium it is — if that’s to be believed, it’s not about any one feature, but instead, it’s about the sum of the experience.

    • Travelers breeze through packing every day, tossing toiletries, snacks, and travel documents into carry-on bags without a second thought.
    • Recent findings suggest that directives from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), USA.gov, and Department of Defense advisories establish clear operational thresholds across identification, liquids, and everyday goods.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travelers breeze through packing every day, tossing toiletries, snacks, and travel documents into carry-on bags without a second thought. As many may have come to realize, routine airport preparation can lead to innocent items being key triggers for secondary security screening, making compliance essential for a smooth journey.

    Recent findings suggest that directives from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), USA.gov, and Department of Defense advisories establish clear operational thresholds across identification, liquids, and everyday goods. Based on official source-validated guidelines and 2026 enforcement rules, this guide breaks down seven commonly misunderstood items that catch unsuspecting passengers off guard at checkpoint lanes.

    According to recent reports, packing a personal firearm for a hunting trip means paying close attention to transport laws, but passengers often make the critical mistake of leaving sidearms tucked inside exterior carry-on compartments. Enforcement data demonstrates that discovering a weapon at the security checkpoint triggers immediate law enforcement intervention and substantial operational disruption.

    The legal and financial fallout of bringing a firearm into a sterile airport area extends far beyond a simple warning or delayed flight. Civil penalties enforced by the agency can reach up to approximately $15,000, accompanied by a mandatory five-year revocation of TSA PreCheck privileges for the offending traveler.

    According to recent reports, preventing these severe penalties means ensuring that any legally transported firearm is completely unloaded, locked inside a hard-sided container, and declared exclusively at the airline check-in counter for checked baggage. These are non-negotiable federal boundaries, so following them helps avoid catastrophic legal consequences before boarding any domestic or international flight.

    According to recent reports, sliding a handy pocket multi-tool with a built-in corkscrew and small blade into an outer pocket feels like harmless vacation prep. However, guidance on sharp object inventories distinguishes strictly between bladeless accessories and bladed tools, prohibiting any sharp edge in the cabin.

    It has been revealed that corkscrews containing integrated blades and standard kitchen knives are universally banned from carry-on compartments, landing them on the immediate confiscation list during X-ray inspection. The only exception granted for knives applies strictly to blunt-edged butter knives, leaving sharp culinary gear purely restricted to checked luggage.

    Industry observers note that many passengers mistakenly place these sharp items in their carry-on, and many are not aware that such items are prohibited, but some try to break the rules. An example of this comes from Dane County, Wisconsin, where a passenger taped a knife to the bottom of their carry-on to avoid paying a checked luggage fee. Ultimately, swapping a bladed corkscrew for a bladeless alternative is a far better option to get seamless passage through screening lanes without risking your personal items.

    Industry observers note that packing a jar of homemade cranberry sauce or a carton of holiday eggnog as a gift for family members is a thoughtful gesture for seasonal travel. However, seasonal advisories categorize spreadable foods, sauces, and liquid beverages under strict volume restrictions that can catch many holiday travelers off guard.

    In a recent development, any liquid food or spread over 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) is strictly prohibited in carry-on luggage and must be transferred to checked bags before you enter the security queue. Wrapped gifts containing festive drinks or preserves will be unwrapped and inspected at the checkpoint belt if they exceed this federal threshold.

    Holiday treats should ideally go into your checked suitcases or, if that is still not possible, opt for solid food alternatives to avoid the frustration of surrendered gifts at terminal security. Federal liquid rules are easy to forget when packing seasonal groceries, and many travelers end up with holiday celebrations that get off to a rough start upon arrival.

    Recent findings suggest that tossing a compact cordless hair styling tool into your carry-on luggage for quick touch-ups upon landing is, no doubt, a convenient way to maintain your grooming routine. Specifications classify cordless butane curling irons under unique operational constraints that require careful attention before packing, so while they may be convenient, they can become problematic for TSA.

    While these styling tools are permitted in carry-on bags, federal safety rules require a secure safety cover that is fitted over the heating element at all times. Furthermore, regulations strictly prohibit carrying spare butane cartridges anywhere in passenger baggage, which makes any uninstalled fuel refills an instant trigger for confiscation.

    According to recent reports, so, while there is no outright ban on these items, checking that specific travel hair tools meet safety requirements before heading to the airport prevents unexpected delays during bag check and X-ray screening. Because these items are also not allowed in checked baggage, checking TSA guidelines is essential when packing.

    Dropping a bulk-sized bottle of contact lens solution into your carry-on toiletry bag is common practice, with many travelers assuming essential medical supplies receive automatic exemptions. While medical exemptions do exist for genuine therapeutic needs, TSA advisories on tsa.gov explicitly warn that certain multi-purpose solutions frequently trigger security alarms during screening.

    According to recent reports, liquid prescription medications are exempt from standard three-one-one volume caps, but they must be explicitly declared to security officers before screening begins. Officers may subject flagged prescription liquids to specialized testing procedures, including vapor analysis, to verify chemical composition and ensure checkpoint safety.

    Informing security personnel about medical liquids and separating them from standard carry-on items speeds up the inspection process for everyone in the traveling party and others in the security queue. Staying informed on medical screening protocols helps manage expectations when traveling with specialized health care supplies. Especially for those with medical reasons that can qualify for a valid exemption, contacting TSA for more information can help avoid any concerns during security checks.

    Packing a large container of post-workout protein powder or a familiar tub of baby powder in your carry-on bag helps maintain your daily routine while traveling. But, according to security guidelines, any powdery substance exceeding 12 ounces (350 milliliters) triggers mandatory separate screening procedures at the security lane.

    If security officers cannot definitively determine the composition of a large powder container during X-ray inspection, the substance may be subject to voluntary or mandatory disposal. This policy aims to maintain cabin safety while also ensuring powdery materials do not obscure underlying organic items on screening monitors.

    Transferring large quantities of powder into smaller containers under 12 ounces (350 milliliters) or packing them into checked luggage can avoid checkpoint restrictions entirely and is a much better option. If you insist on keeping protein powders in your checked luggage, then preparing your powdered items correctly ensures you avoid secondary screening delays and potential product disposal at the terminal.

    Grabbing your standard state driver's license, tossing it into your wallet, and heading straight for airport security assumes your identification is fully compliant with federal standards. However, strict enforcement of the REAL ID Act is active, meaning non-compliant state licenses no longer grant unverified passage.

    It has been revealed that for travelers caught without a REAL ID, the TSA ConfirmID program, which rolled out in February 2026, has a $45 fee for a 10-day validity window. Documentation from the Defense Travel Management Office notes that this fee is non-reimbursable for official travel, and TSA rules require showing either an electronic or printed proof-of-payment receipt at the checkpoint.

    Industry observers note that ensuring your identification meets federal requirements well before you arrive at the airport is the most reliable way to prevent checkpoint rejections and boarding delays. Keeping digital or printed payment receipts readily accessible when using temporary compliance programs helps ensure a smooth transition through security.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A very small international airline plans to add long haul, international flights to the United States as of next spring, and I feel pretty confident in saying that 99% of people have never heard of this airline (I had to look it up after seeing one of their planes at an airport several weeks back, and I know a thing or two about identifying airplanes). 😉.

    Sources indicate that as reported by AeroRoutes, as of May 1, 2027, Parata Air will launch daily nonstop flights between Seoul Incheon (ICN) and Los Angeles (LAX). The flight will operate with the following schedule:.

    WE301 Incheon to Los Angeles departing 12:00PM arriving 7:20AMWE302 Los Angeles to Incheon departing 9:50AM arriving 3:20PM (+1 days).

    Parata Air will operate the route with an Airbus A330-200, featuring 260 seats, including 18 business class seats and 242 economy seats. The 5,944-mile flight is blocked at 11hr40min eastbound and 13hr30min westbound.

    Tickets on the flight are now on sale, and I see fares starting at around $670 one-way in economy, and around $2,500 one-way in business class. Those aren’t exactly terribly attractive fares for a newcomer that appears to have a pretty lackluster onboard product.

    In a recent development, for those not familiar with Parata Air, the airline released operations back in 2019, but it has a fleet of just a handful of planes, including three Airbus A330s and two Airbus A320s. This will be the carrier’s first service outside of Asia. As I hinted at in the headline, I imagine this is a fully unknown player to most people, and I had never heard of the airline until a few weeks ago.

    In a recent development, random thought — can anyone think of a smaller international airline (in terms of fleet size) that added long haul flights to the United States? I know that’s very specific, but I can’t think of another one… it’s possible I’m missing something, though!

    The airline acquired its three A330s secondhand from different sources, with the planes having flown for Garuda Indonesia, Hainan Airlines, and Thomas Cook (though that plane doesn’t have business class).

    The Seoul Incheon to Los Angeles market is pretty well served in terms of capacity, but not so well served in terms of competition. That’s because no US carrier flies between Los Angeles and Seoul Incheon, and with Korean Air having acquired Asiana, there’s now only one South Korean flag carrier.

    If you look at the market, you’ll see that Korean Air operates up to four daily flights, and Air Premia operates up to two daily flights. Now we’ll see a third airline from the country operating in the market, though with the lowest capacity, and arguably the worst product.

    It’ll be interesting to see when we see some competition here on the US side. Delta might operate the route eventually, but that doesn’t actually increase competition, since the airline has a joint venture with Korean Air. American has (smartly, probably) given up on Los Angeles as a long haul hub. So that leaves United, and I could definitely see the airline eventually adding service in the market, as a competitive response against Delta and Korean Air, if nothing else.

    In a recent development, as of May 2027, Parata Air will be launching a upcoming nonstop route between Seoul Incheon and Los Angeles, representing the carrier’s first service outside of Asia. The airline will be operating daily in the market with Airbus A330s. With this, there will be three South Korean carriers flying this route, though no airlines from the United States.
