    #42278. Frontier's GoWild All You Can Fly pass is back with no blackout dates and earlier booking

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (691 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    Frontier's GoWild All You Can Fly pass is back with no blackout dates and earlier booking

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Frontier Airlines is now offering its GoWild All You Can Fly Pass for 2027, letting travelers take to the skies at a deep discount for an entire year (and potentially longer).
    • Industry observers note that for a limited time, flyers can purchase a GoWild Pass good through 2027 for just $399.
    • While that's not quite as good as some offers we've seen in past years (but better than some in other years), it can add up to significant savings if you fly the airline a lot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's here! Frontier Airlines is now offering its GoWild All You Can Fly Pass for 2027, letting travelers take to the skies at a deep discount for an entire year (and potentially longer).

    Industry observers note that for a limited time, flyers can purchase a GoWild Pass good through 2027 for just $399. Members of the airline's Discount Den can score the pass for $349.

    While that's not quite as good as some offers we've seen in past years (but better than some in other years), it can add up to significant savings if you fly the airline a lot. You must be a Frontier Miles member to purchase one.

    Keep in mind that passholders pay $0.01 in airfare plus applicable taxes, fees and charges at the time of booking, so the pass gets you out of the regular airfare, but you're still on the hook for taxes and fees as well as other charges for things like optional seat selection and bags. While taxes on domestic legs are low, international ones can incur $60-$110 each way, depending on the destination.

    Sneak peek: Frontier's newly introduced first-class seats are finally on sale, set for March debut.

    Multiple passholders can book travel at the same time, but you can't mix and match passholders with non-passholders on the same reservation.

    Likewise, different types of fares can be combined each way on itineraries as long as all passengers hold a valid GoWild Pass at the time of booking and the primary passenger holds a Discount Den membership if Discount Den fares are selected.

    Recent findings suggest that one other big caveat: GoWild passes autorenew, so if you want to cancel when your current pass expires, you'll need to contact the airline to do so. Your renewal date will be stated in your confirmation email when purchasing the pass.

    According to recent reports, the GoWild Pass is valid for flights to over 100 destinations across Frontier's route network, including both domestic gateways and international cities in Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America. The airline's route network changes frequently, though, so stay on top of it to make sure your route will be in service when it's time to book.

    It has been revealed that travel begins after purchase (meaning as soon as today) and is available through Dec. 31, 2027, meaning potentially over a full year of flying.

    There are no blackout dates, like we've seen in some past instances, but on peak dates, you can expect to pay $59-$199 extra per segment.

    Industry observers note that here's the kicker: Standard bookings for eligible GoWild fares begin a day before departure for domestic flights and 10 days before departure for international flights. If your return flight is outside that window, then you'll have to try to make an additional booking when the window opens for that flight.

    If you do want to book more in advance than that, however, you can pay an additional charge to do so, though this can vary based on the date and the route.

    Also keep in mind that just because a seat is open on the flight you want does not mean it's eligible for a GoWild booking.

    You can earn Frontier Miles on the purchase of the pass as well as any extras, like seat assignments, bag fees or priority boarding that you purchase.

    If you hold elite status with Frontier, you are still eligible for your benefits, including free seats and bags, so that can be a great way to save on optional fees that non-elites have to pay.

    All-you-can-fly airline passes are a rarity these days and come with lots of limitations. Frontier Airlines' GoWild All You Can Fly Pass is no exception.

    According to recent reports, still, if you fly the airline a lot, have flexibility (and a bit of spontaneity) in your plans and don't need a ton of extra amenities like preferred seats or checked bags, these fares can be a good way to save a bit on flights you'd be taking anyway ... or perhaps some fun last-minute fares you wouldn't be able to take advantage of otherwise.

    #42277. Industry News: Park Hyatt Brisbane Opening 2031, As Brand’s Fourth Australia Hotel

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1040 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Park Hyatt Brisbane Opening 2031, As Brand’s Fourth Australia Hotel

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, hyatt will bring its luxury Park Hyatt brand to Brisbane, Australia.
    • Sources indicate that hyatt has unveiled prepares for the Park Hyatt Brisbane, marking the brand’s debut in Queensland.
    • The hotel will occupy the top floors of one of the two towers of the 309 North Quay, a mixed-use development also containing luxury homes and retail outlets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, hyatt will bring its luxury Park Hyatt brand to Brisbane, Australia. More Park Hyatt locations are always a good thing, but… well, let’s cover the details first.

    Sources indicate that hyatt has unveiled prepares for the Park Hyatt Brisbane, marking the brand’s debut in Queensland. The hotel is expected to open in 2031, and will be located on the shores of the Brisbane River, at the western edge of the city’s central business district.

    The hotel will occupy the top floors of one of the two towers of the 309 North Quay, a mixed-use development also containing luxury homes and retail outlets. For what it’s worth, the two buildings will have 51 floors and 56 floors. The hotel will have 201 guest rooms and suites, offering views of the river and skyline, along with 50 serviced apartments, for extended residence.

    In a recent development, there are no additional details about the property yet. I do appreciate that the hotel will at least be at the top of a building, as that should make for some very nice views (I hate when hotels are part of tall buildings, but then take up the bottom floors, as that’s becoming increasingly common).

    While a 2031 opening is expected, I would definitely not count on that timeline sticking. Ground hasn’t even broken on this development, and these kinds of mixed-use developments tend to struggle with sticking to their planned timeline.

    Here’s how Tamara Lohan, Hyatt’s Global Brand Leader for Luxury, describes this:.

    “The Park Hyatt calling cards have always been iconic design and extraordinary addresses. Brisbane has the confidence and growing global pull to make it a natural home for the brand. When it opens, Park Hyatt Brisbane will become the fifth Park Hyatt hotel in the Pacific, joining hotels in Sydney, Melbourne, Canberra and Auckland, and a deliberate next step in growing the brand in the right places.”.

    There are no renderings of the property yet, beyond the below one of the overall 309 North Quay development.

    This will be the fourth Park Hyatt property in Australia, and the fifth in the South Pacific, complementing the properties in Auckland, Canberra, Melbourne, and Sydney. I don’t have the slightest clue what’s going on with the Canberra property, as my understanding is that it’s not up to Park Hyatt standards, so it’s marketed as “Hyatt Hotel Canberra – A Park Hyatt Hotel.” So it is a Park Hyatt, or is it not a Park Hyatt?

    World of Hyatt is my favorite major hotel loyalty program (though the lead is narrowing as of late), and Park Hyatt is probably my favorite Hyatt brand. 15 years ago, the brand got me really excited, because it had some really spectacular properties. But it just feels like the brand is sort of losing steam, especially when you compare the difference in trajectory between Park Hyatt and Waldorf Astoria. My frustration with Park Hyatt comes down to two things.

    First, the brand just seemingly can’t pick up many “flagship” properties, or at least can’t maintain them. Look at the world’s biggest business markets and most iconic cities — we’re talking Hong Kong, London, Latest York, Paris, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, etc. There are no Park Hyatts in places like Hong Kong or Singapore, and the ones that have historically been pretty iconic just fall short of actually being the top properties in their cities:.

    Recent findings suggest that the area where Park Hyatt has been doing well in recent times is in secondary cities, at least in comparison to the above. And this isn’t meant to be shade — I’d much rather hang out in Auckland or Kuala Lumpur than in London or New York (take your pitchforks elsewhere!), but there’s no denying that any true luxury hotel brand wants to have world class properties in those primary cities.

    Recent findings suggest that I just feel like as of late, Waldorf Astoria’s trajectory has been way more impressive than Park Hyatt’s, and I’m not sure what exactly is driving that. I feel like owners just aren’t as into developing Park Hyatts as they used to be. Is there a single Park Hyatt in the pipeline where I think “oh, this is going to be a best-in-class property in a major market?” I can’t think of any….

    Recent findings suggest that the Park Hyatt brand is coming to Brisbane, Australia, with a hotel expected to open in 2031. The 201-key property will be located on the top floors of a mixed-use development, which will also contain apartments and retail.

    It’s cool to see more Park Hyatts in the pipeline, and I don’t want to knock the brand for expanding to more markets. I’m just disappointed that the Park Hyatt brand can’t pick up any steam in the biggest cities, in terms of delivering an actually competitive experience.

    What do you make of aims for the Park Hyatt Brisbane?

    Tech Report: Chase Adds Qantas And Cathay Pacific Transfers—More Access To Premium Award Seats

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • Chase is adding Qantas and Cathay Pacific as 1:1 transfer partners on November 18.
    • Sources indicate that these are Chase’s first latest airline transfer partners in more than five years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    Chase is adding Qantas and Cathay Pacific as 1:1 transfer partners on November 18. For me, the biggest value is access to business and first class award seats that these airlines don’t make available to members of other frequent flyer programs.

    Sources indicate that these are Chase’s first latest airline transfer partners in more than five years. And they’re an unambiguously positive addition, even if neither becomes the program most cardmembers use most often.

    Eligible cards include Chase Sapphire Reserve, Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve for Business, Ink Business Preferred and J.P. Morgan Reserve. Both newly introduced partners transfer at 1:1. Hyatt transfers are now less generous for Sapphire Preferred and Ink Business Preferred: 4 Chase points become 3 Hyatt points, while the Reserve cards retain 1:1. That distinction doesn’t apply to these new airline partners. Chase Sapphire Reserve® (See rates and fees) is a strong card for actual spending, with 4 points per dollar on flights and hotels booked directly and 3 points per dollar on dining. Adding more transfer partners makes the value of those points even greater. Why I Want Qantas Points Chase already had ways to book oneworld flights through programs like British Airways and Iberia. But being able to book an airline doesn’t mean having access to all of its award seats. Airlines increasingly keep more of their premium cabin availability for their own members. As I explained when Rove added Qantas transfers, Qantas offers its members award space that American AAdvantage, Alaska and British Airways members can’t book. I have family in Australia and have had real success finding Qantas business class awards when there’s flexibility over the U.S. gateway and travel date. I’ll set alerts across several flights rather than insist on one. Some flight between Australia and the U.S. will inevitably open up with a couple of business class awards, usually around 60 days out. Qantas can also be useful for Emirates redemptions. I’d generally rather book the same available Emirates business class seat through Copa ConnectMiles, though. Copa charges 80,000 miles one way between the U.S. and Dubai in business class without fuel surcharges. And Qantas is no longer an unrestricted way around Emirates’ first class award limits. Booking Emirates first class with Qantas points requires Qantas Silver status or higher, and passengers must be at least nine years old. Cathay Offers More Award Space And Lower British Airways Surcharges Cathay Pacific is similar. Its own members get access to far more premium cabin award space than members of partner programs. Asia Miles prices can be high, though. I also like Asia Miles for reducing fuel surcharges on British Airways awards, particularly compared with booking through American AAdvantage. It’s also notable that Chase’s Cathay transfer rate is better than American Express’s. American Express transfers 1,000 Membership Rewards points to just 800 Asia Miles. An award requiring 100,000 Asia Miles takes 100,000 Chase points versus 125,000 Amex points (without transfer bonus). American Express, Citi, Capital One and Rove already partner with both Qantas and Cathay. Chase is catching up with these. I wouldn’t transfer points just because these options have been added. Chase Is Finally Adding Airline Partners Again Chase’s last new transfer partner was Wyndham Rewards in February 2026. Its last new airline partner was Air Canada Aeroplan on August 3, 2021. I welcomed Wyndham because it showed Chase was building out Ultimate Rewards, even though I had little interest in transferring points there. Qantas and Cathay are programs I can see myself using. They bring Chase to 12 airline transfer programs and four hotel programs. I also wonder whether these relationships could lead to more Points Boost opportunities. With Points Boost, Chase can use discounts it negotiates on paid tickets to offer more value per point through its travel portal. More airline relationships could help them offer more flights, more dates, or better redemption values. Qantas has already appeared in Points Boost, and American Airlines has participated without being a Chase transfer partner. But I’d love to see deeper relationships produce more opportunities to redeem at 2 cents per point for premium cabin tickets in the future.     #42274. Tech Report: World Of Hyatt Status Revamps For 2027—Award Stacking And Upcoming Benefit Choices, But Cuts Come Also

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5998 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: World Of Hyatt Status Revamps For 2027—Award Stacking And Upcoming Benefit Choices, But Cuts Come Also

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • Recent findings suggest that hyatt will finally let members combine a free night certificate with a confirmed suite upgrade starting January 1, 2027.
    • Recent findings suggest that this isn’t an across the board improvement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    Recent findings suggest that hyatt will finally let members combine a free night certificate with a confirmed suite upgrade starting January 1, 2027. I’ve wanted that for years. They’re also extending milestone free night certificates from 180 days to a year, and adding rewards after just 10 qualifying nights.

    Recent findings suggest that this isn’t an across the board improvement. Suite upgrades will expire sooner. The suite upgrade choice at 50 nights gets cut in half. And My Hyatt Concierge becomes something you select alongside other rewards, rather than something everyone automatically receives at 60 nights. Free parking will no longer be an automatic benefit on award stays for Globalists.

    Recent findings suggest that when I covered Hyatt’s last major status benefit refresh in November 2023, I liked it overall. They made awards transferable, added choices, and let members try Globalist benefits before earning Globalist. Guest of Honor became limited, but the Milestone Rewards themselves mostly got better.

    This time there are upcoming and better options. I genuinely like a lot of the choices, but there are real tradeoffs. Hyatt is pitching the changes as more choice and flexibility, based on listening to members. That’s actually fair for much of this, though I don’t think members told them what they really wanted was for suite upgrade to expire up to a year earlier.

    Hyatt will allow members to combine eligible awards on the same reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and the newly introduced Free Parking Awards. This fixes one of the problems I’ve been complaining about for years. A free night certificate is something you often want to use on a special leisure stay. That’s also when a suite may matter most, especially traveling with family. When I didn’t want to use a free night certificate was a work trip by myself. Free night awards had a lot less value to me because I had to give up a confirmed suite to use them. But being able to use the two awards together makes both more valuable. Combining Guest of Honor with a suite upgrade is useful, too. You can give someone Globalist treatment and confirm their suite ahead of time, rather than leaving the room upgrade to availability when they arrive. Hyatt also promises an enhanced Pay My Way experience, letting members mix awards, points, cash and Points + Cash by night. Online selection, gifting and redemption will be available for eligible awards. Pay My Way and stacking, by the way, really do all work together. Hyatt offers me this illustration, Let’s say a member is making a three night booking. Assuming both the Standard Suite was available for the duration, and there is award inventory available on the selected dates (just like today) – yes, a member could apply a Suite Upgrade Award to the whole stay, a Free Parking award to the whole stay, a Guest of Honor Award to the whole stay, and then pay for the reservation using points on one night, a promotional Free Night Award on another night, and cash on the third night.

    Hyatt will allow members to combine eligible awards on the same reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and the fresh Free Parking Awards.

    According to recent reports, this fixes one of the problems I’ve been complaining about for years. A free night certificate is something you often want to use on a special leisure stay. That’s also when a suite may matter most, especially traveling with family. When I didn’t want to use a free night certificate was a work trip by myself. Free night awards had a lot less value to me because I had to give up a confirmed suite to use them. But being able to use the two awards together makes both more valuable.

    Combining Guest of Honor with a suite upgrade is useful, too. You can give someone Globalist treatment and confirm their suite ahead of time, rather than leaving the room upgrade to availability when they arrive.

    Hyatt also promises an enhanced Pay My Way experience, letting members mix awards, points, cash and Points + Cash by night. Online selection, gifting and redemption will be available for eligible awards. Pay My Way and stacking, by the way, really do all work together. Hyatt offers me this illustration,.

    Let’s say a member is making a three night booking. Assuming both the Standard Suite was available for the duration, and there is award inventory available on the selected dates (just like today) – yes, a member could apply a Suite Upgrade Award to the whole stay, a Free Parking award to the whole stay, a Guest of Honor Award to the whole stay, and then pay for the reservation using points on one night, a promotional Free Night Award on another night, and cash on the third night.

    Milestone Rewards currently begin at 20 qualifying nights. Next year they’ll start at 10 nights or 20,000 base points. Here’s the new chart through 50 nights. Qualifying nights / base points   What you receive 10 / 20,000   Choose one: 1 qualifying night credit, $25 FIND experience credit, or $30 Inclusive Collection spa credit. 20 / 35,000   Choose one: 2 qualifying night credits, $30 spa credit, $25 Delta certificate, 2K Next Stay Award, or 2 Club Access Awards. 30 / 50,000   Choose 10,000 bonus points or a Category 1–4 free night. Also choose one: 2 qualifying night credits, $30 spa credit, $25 Delta certificate, 2K Next Stay Award, or 2 Club Access Awards. 40 / 65,000   Receive 1 Guest of Honor Award. Also choose one: 5 qualifying night credits, $200 Thompson Hotels credit, $75 Delta certificate, 5,000 points, or 1 Suite Upgrade Award. 50 / 80,000   Choose one: $200 Thompson Hotels credit, $75 Delta certificate, 5,000 points, or 1 Suite Upgrade Award. The qualifying night choices add up to 10 nights: one at the first milestone, two at the next, two at 30 nights and five at 40 nights. These count toward both status and Milestone Rewards. That creates a path to Globalist with 50 qualifying nights from other sources, if you select all four night rewards. The requirement remains 60, but 10 can come from these choices. And you earn qualifying nights with the The World Of Hyatt Credit Card (See rates and fees) too – 5 qualifying night credits every year and 2 qualifying night every time you spend $5,000 on the card. The 30 night option to take 10,000 points instead of a Category 1–4 certificate is useful for someone who struggles to use the certificate. A good Category 4 redemption can be worth more, and the certificate will become easier to use with the longer expiration and ability to add a suite upgrade. One Fewer Suite Upgrade, And A Choice About Your Concierge The reduction at 50 nights is easy to miss. The current choice is two Suite Upgrade Awards. The new chart offers one. At 60 nights or 100,000 base points, members will receive: 2 Guest of Honor Awards. A choice of free nights: 2 Category 1–4 awards or 1 Category 1–7 award. Two selections from this menu: 7,500 bonus points, a Free Parking Award, a $100 Delta certificate, 2 Suite Upgrade Awards, or My Hyatt Concierge. You can still select the two suite upgrades and concierge access, keeping the existing 60 night package. But if you want points or parking, something else has to go. And you can’t make the same two choices at 60 nights – you can’t have four upgrades, 15,000 points or two parking awards. You don’t have o select all of your awards at once, though you do have to make these two selections at the same time. Hyatt explains to me that you’ll still have 90 days to make your choices, and: In milestones where there are separate choices, such as 30 nights, the member can make those choices at different points within the 90 day selection window (e.g., could choose the Free Night Award one day, and the HIC Spa credit on a different day.) At 60 nights, the member can choose their free night award choice on a different day from the other selection, but the two selections within “Choose Two” must be made together at the same time. I do plan to keep the concierge benefit, even though mine has never been very responsive. I won’t give up the ability to email someone to address issues. I just wish I would hear back more rapidly, and didn’t need to follow up so often. Maybe that’s actually coming? Hyatt tells me they do plan greater investment in the concierge program: [B]y shifting to a choice, we will be able to further invest in My Hyatt Concierge and deliver even more proactive and personalized care. We will share more when available.

At 60 nights, the member can choose their free night award choice on a different day from the other selection, but the two selections within “Choose Two” must be made together at the same time.

    As before, lifetime Globalists retain their concierge without having to stay 60 nights.

A Year To Use Every Award Is Both An Improvement And A Cut Hyatt’s release presents the new expiration policy as giving members extra time. That’s true for some awards, but the effect runs in both directions. Hyatt tells me, For all awards issued on January 1, 2027 or later, expiration dates will be 365 days from the date of issuance. Milestone free night awards that currently expire after 180 days will get substantially more time. But suite upgrades, ordinary Milestone Guest of Honor awards and club access awards currently have much longer lives, generally through the end of the year earned plus another 14 months under Hyatt’s existing rules. A suite upgrade selected January 1, 2026 remained valid through February 2028. Under a 365 day rule, the same issuance date would produce a January 1, 2027 expiration. That’s more than a year of usefulness gone. Shortening the window makes it harder to hold upgrades for a major trip, to book far ahead, or to save awards from a heavy travel year for a quieter one. Note that this change applies to Milestone Rewards earned starting in 2027. So any that you earn at the end of 2026, and redeem in 2027, follow the old rules. Hyatt confirms, Only awards earned and selected after January 1, 2027 follow the new 365 expiration from issuance. So, a 2026 award (even if selected in 2027) would carry the current 2026 expiration rules. Also choose one: Delta Gold Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. 110, 120, 130 and 140, at each milestone   1 Guest of Honor Award, plus choose one: Delta Gold Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. 150   Choose 2 Category 1–7 nights or an Ultimate Free Night Award. Also choose one: Delta Platinum Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. The Ultimate Free Night at 150 nights isn’t going away. The two Category 1–7 nights are an alternative. Someone who wants two nights at less expensive hotels can choose those, while someone planning one especially expensive night can retain the Ultimate award, which covers participating Category 1–8 hotels, Category A–F all-inclusives and Miraval. The new hotel credits are more restrictive than points: $30 Inclusive Collection spa credit: for spa treatments at participating all-inclusive resorts. $200 Thompson Hotels credit: toward an eligible paid stay. $500 premium suite credit: toward an eligible paid premium suite stay of at least two nights. I’ve wanted a way to use two suite upgrades to confirm a premium suite. A discount on buying a premium suite isn’t as attractive to me. But there are times I might use it. What Hyatt Gets From These Changes The strongest improvements are award stacking, more time to use free night certificates, an earlier first reward, and choices that let members avoid awards they won’t use. A member who doesn’t value concierge access can get something else, while someone who prefers two less expensive hotel nights can choose them. I expect members approaching Globalist will like the qualifying night choices. People who lose free night certificates to expiration should come out ahead, too. Existing Globalists who use all their suite upgrades, plan trips far ahead, or regularly choose FIND experiences have more to lose. Hyatt also gets more ways to influence where members spend. A Thompson credit encourages a paid Thompson stay. A spa credit encourages a treatment that may cost much more than the credit. The premium suite credit encourages someone to buy a room they might otherwise try to upgrade into. Shorter suite award validity should leave fewer outstanding upgrades available for future use. Making concierge elective lets members reveal whether they value the service more than points or another reward. And offering status credits makes the next milestone feel closer, encouraging someone with a modest number of Hyatt nights to keep going. For me, being able to confirm a suite on a free night certificate is the biggest improvement. I care much more about that than a spa coupon. There really is more choice and the ability to earn status faster with these changes. Stacking and combining rewards is great. So is longer expiration of free night awards, though sadly at the cost of shorter expiration for suite upgrade awards. The most consequential change for me might be something that isn’t really being announced. If changing My Hyatt Concierge to a choice benefit really does entail greater investment in the program, it would make the experience far more premium and secure even greater loyalty.     #42273. Fun & Creative Airline Callsigns, From Shamrock To Starwalker

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1297 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Fun & Creative Airline Callsigns, From Shamrock To Starwalker

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Here’s a fun topic for aviation geeks (so if you’re not one, feel free to skip this post)….
    • When pilots and air traffic controllers communicate, they have a callsign that they use to be identified.
    • It has been revealed that in general aviation, that callsign is just the aircraft’s registration code, so it’s always the same for a particular aircraft.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Here’s a fun topic for aviation geeks (so if you’re not one, feel free to skip this post)….

    When pilots and air traffic controllers communicate, they have a callsign that they use to be identified.

    It has been revealed that in general aviation, that callsign is just the aircraft’s registration code, so it’s always the same for a particular aircraft. For example, if the plane has the registration code N111PG, it would be spoken as “November One One One Papa Golf.”.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile for commercial aircraft, the callsign consists of a organization identifier plus the flight number. In some cases that company identifier is simply the company’s name, while in other cases, a different callsign is used. For example, for American, Delta, and United, the company identifier is simply the airline name, so American flight 100 would be spoken as “American 100.”.

    According to recent reports, in some situations, airlines choose callsigns that are different from the tech giant name, and this can be for a variety of reasons. Callsigns need to be approved by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), with some crucial considerations:.

    While most airlines simply use their name as their callsign, there are also some airlines that don’t, and there are some names that I find to be particularly fun. In this post, I’d like to share my favorite airline callsigns, with a little backstory on how they were chosen (as I understand it). In no particular order….

    Aer Lingus’ callsign is “Shamrock,” and that’s because the shamrock is the national symbol of Ireland. It’s a key part of the airline’s corporate identity, down to the shamrock being featured on the tails of Aer Lingus planes.

    British Airways’ callsign is “Speedbird,” and I’d argue it’s perhaps the most iconic callsign out there. The origin of this dates back to British Airways’ predecessor, Imperial Airways, which used the stylized bird logo. British Airways has been using the callsign since it was founded in 1974 (as a combination of predecessors).

    It has been revealed that while this is of course a creative callsign, it has a practical use as well. “British Airways” would’ve been too long of a callsign, and “British” would’ve likely been too generic. For example, British Midland (which ended up being merged into British Airways) used “Midland” as its callsign, to avoid confusion.

    Recent findings suggest that republic Airways’ callsign is “Brickyard,” and it’s probably the coolest callsign you’ll find at an airline in the United States. The callsign is a tribute to the manufacturer’s headquarters in Indianapolis, also home to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. The course was initially paved with three million bricks, and nicknamed “The Brickyard.”.

    For those not familiar, Republic operates flights on behalf of the regional subsidiaries of the major US carriers, so this is among the most common callsigns you’ll hear on air traffic control frequencies in the US.

    PSA Airlines’ callsign is “Blue Streak,” and after Republic, it’s probably the coolest callsign you’ll find at an airline in the United States. The story behind this callsign is definitely a blast from the past. In the 1980s, PSA’s predecessor was Jetstream International Airlines, and it operated commuter flights as a Piedmont Commuter feeder carrier.

    The carrier’s planes had a white fuselage with a prominent blue stripe along it, intended to match Piedmont Airlines’ livery, and that’s where it all started.

    Recent findings suggest that for those not familiar, PSA operates flights on behalf of the regional subsidiaries of the major US carriers, so this is also a very common callsign that you’ll hear. Given the lack of blue stripes nowadays, the callsign does tend to cause some confusion!

    China Airlines’ callsign is “Dynasty.” It’s my understanding that the Taiwan-based carrier had to choose a non-obvious callsign both to avoid confusion (given the number of airlines with “China” in their name), and also with the intent of differentiating it from mainland China.

    Recent findings suggest that so, where did the dynasty term come from? China Airlines uses this branding pretty widely, with its frequent flyer program even being named Dynasty Flyer, and it’s intended to reflect the history of Taiwan.

    According to recent reports, starlux Airlines’ callsign is “Starwalker.” The reason is because the “Starlux” callsign was already taken by Comlux Aruba, a tiny charter airline, before the Taiwanese airline was founded. Now, don’t ask me why Comlux Aruba has “Starlux” as its callsign, though!

    According to recent reports, the reason Starlux ended up with “Starwalker” is presumably because the company’s founder is a huge Star Wars fan, which is why many things about the airline have space branding. He’s also of course a huge aviation geek, and operates flights as a captain!

    South African Airways’ callsign is “Springbok.” The reason is because “South African” would be too long of a callsign, so they selected the springbok, which is the national animal of South Africa. The carrier has also used this in its branding over the years. For example, back in the 1950s, the airline used “Springbok Service” to describe its long haul, flagship flights.

    Atlas Air’s callsign is “Giant.” Huh, say what? For those not familiar, Atlas Air is a cargo and charter airline, and while it doesn’t operate regularly scheduled commercial flights, it is a big operation.

    Sources indicate that the callsign is presumably a reflection of the firm’s name coming from Greek mythology, where “Atlas” was a titan of great strength, so that may also explain the “giant” callsign. Now, it’s worth mentioning that Atlas also flies some pretty “giant” planes, as the world’s largest Boeing 747 operator, but I don’t think that’s the primary motivation.

    Kalitta Air’s callsign is “Connie.” For those not familiar, Kalitta Air is a cargo airline with a few dozen planes (most of which are Boeing 747s!). The callsign is named after the company’s founder, Conrad “Connie” Kalitta, who started the airline back in 1967, as Connie Kalitta Services.

    European Air Transport’s callsign is “Postman.” For context, this is one of DHL’s European subsidiaries operating cargo flights, so it’s a pretty fitting callsign, eh?

    Airlines have callsigns that they use to communicate with air traffic control. While most airlines simply use their name as their callsign, that’s not always the case. In some situations a different name has to be chosen for practical reasons, while in some cases airlines want to get creative. I love when airlines have some fun with this, so I figured it was worth a post.

    What’s your favorite airline callsign?

    Fun fact: in Heathrow, the address of BA's headquarters is "Speedbird Way" :-).

    KM Malta Airlines uses the callsign SkyKnight. KM stands for Knights of Malta and was the 2 letter code for the former Air Malta.

    i love BermudAir's - gosling - as i'm a huge fan of birds.

    When Tiger Airways was flying domestically in Australia, its call sign was "Go Cat" which is a local cat food brand :).

    It has been revealed that at Monday night’s Rutgers College Republicans event, protesters began shouting within minutes of Bovino taking the stage.     Sherrill said that if the club went ahead with the event, she would ensure the state worked with Rutgers to protect "the safety of everyone and the rights enshrined in our Constitution," and she urged attendees to question Bovino about his record.

    #42271. Breaking: No more permanent coalitions: What the midterm results reveal

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (908 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: No more permanent coalitions: What the midterm results reveal

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 9 for a group photo with incoming members of his caucus: from left, Ohio's Sherrod Brown, Texas' James Talarico, Iowa's Josh Turek, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed, North Carolina's Roy Cooper, Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Newly introduced Hampshire's Chris Pappas, South Carolina's Annie Andrews, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, Maine's Troy Jackson and Kansas' Adam Hamilton.
    • ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once stated.
    • In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer poses in his office on Nov. 9 for a group photo with incoming members of his caucus: from left, Ohio's Sherrod Brown, Texas' James Talarico, Iowa's Josh Turek, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed, North Carolina's Roy Cooper, Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Newly introduced Hampshire's Chris Pappas, South Carolina's Annie Andrews, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, Maine's Troy Jackson and Kansas' Adam Hamilton. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

    ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once stated. “If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.”.

    In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness. Republicans had captured the White House, flipped the Senate and held the House. President Donald Trump had completely altered the party coalitions as he led the ascendant GOP to victory.

    Now, just two years later, Democrats are on the rise. A historic midterm tsunami has swept them into such commanding Senate and House majorities that some are questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again. And if Texas is blue, how does the GOP have any chance in the Electoral College again?

    A big takeaway from the midterm results should be that there’s very little permanence in our politics.

    What may have looked like a new GOP coalition was really more of a Trump coalition, and it crumbled in the face of economic frustrations, affordability concerns and the president’s unpopular policies.

    With Trump’s negative job approval rating weighing them down, Republican candidates suffered losses among virtually all demographic groups – including by wide margins among constituencies thought to make up the GOP’s core.

    It has been revealed that trump or the Republicans finished ahead among male voters by 4 points in 2018, 8 points in 2020, 14 points in 2022 and 12 points in 2024, according to the exit polls. Men went for Democratic candidates by 4 points (51 percent to 47 percent) this cycle. Meanwhile, Republicans lost even more ground among women. While Kamala Harris finished ahead of Trump by 8 points in 2024, that margin grew to 21 points for Democratic candidates this year.

    Sources indicate that trump closed the gap among Hispanic voters to just 5 points behind Harris two years ago. This year, Hispanic voters nationwide supported Democratic candidates by 32 points (65 percent to 33 percent). Even white voters shifted significantly. They backed Trump or  Republican candidates by 10 points in 2018, 17 points in 2020, 18 points in 2022 and 15 points in 2024. And yet Democrats edged out Republicans by a point (50 percent to 49 percent) on Nov. 3.

    Industry observers note that voters without a college degree were supposed to be a key cog in Republicans’ latest populist coalition. But they went from +13 (56 percent to 43 percent) for Trump in 2024 to backing Republican candidates by just 1 point this year. Meanwhile, the gap among voters with a college degree went from 14 points for Harris in 2024 to 30 points for Democrats this cycle.

    It has been revealed that republicans had closed the gap among young voters aged 18 to 29 from 35 points in 2018 to just 11 points in 2024. But younger voters supported Democratic candidates this year by 50 points (74 percent to 24 percent). Not to mention Democrats flipped voters aged 45 to 64 for the first time in nearly two decades.

    White evangelicals appear to be one of the only groups that didn’t shift toward Democrats. They supported GOP candidates 82 percent to 17 percent. But they only made up 17 percent of the electorate, according to the exit polls, which is down from a very consistent 25 percent for more than a decade. So there was still a problem with that group of voters, but it was more about turnout than persuasion.

    Industry observers note that while there was an unmistakable leftward shift this year, the results should not be considered a permanent party realignment any more than 2024 was. While Democrats did extremely well in Texas this year, they still haven’t won the Lone Star State in a presidential race in 50 years. So maybe it’s wise for everyone to take a deep breath.

    If you take this year’s election results and match them with the Senate seats on the ballot in 2028, there doesn’t appear to be a viable path for Republicans back to the majority. But there wasn’t a particularly viable Democratic path to the Senate majority at this point two years ago. And if the Alaska election goes their way, they will end up winning Senate races in seven states that were initially rated Solid Republican.

    According to recent reports, if one party starts to get too comfortable, voters have a way of bringing politicians back down to earth. If Democrats come to Congress and push too far to the left or become too defined by their most extreme members, they will squander the opportunity they earned this year.

    The dramatic demographic swings should be evidence that many voters are not beholden to either party and are open to switching allegiances, particularly in a time of economic uncertainty.

    At the same time, if Republicans don’t go through some time of reflection and instead triple down on the policies that led to the blue wave, they risk cementing some of the shifts that started this cycle. It just won’t be thick cement.

    LATAM Unveils Fresh Airbus A321XLR Business Class Suites, Coming March 2027

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1143 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, LATAM has just unveiled the full interiors for its upcoming Airbus A321XLRs, which will make it the first carrier in South America to offer fully flat suites with direct aisle access on a narrow body aircraft.
    • LATAM has 13 Airbus A321XLRs are on order, which are expected to enter service as of March 2027.
    • In a recent development, the airline intends to use these planes to open up new long haul markets, though it’s not yet clear out of which LATAM hubs the planes will fly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, LATAM has just unveiled the full interiors for its upcoming Airbus A321XLRs, which will make it the first carrier in South America to offer fully flat suites with direct aisle access on a narrow body aircraft. These planes are expected to enter service in the coming months, so we won’t have to wait much longer to fly them!

    LATAM has 13 Airbus A321XLRs are on order, which are expected to enter service as of March 2027. The A321XLR is the latest long range, narrow body aircraft from Airbus, which stretches the capabilities of the A321 family.

    In a recent development, the airline intends to use these planes to open up new long haul markets, though it’s not yet clear out of which LATAM hubs the planes will fly. I suspect these planes will primarily be used for service to North America, or possibly for service from secondary cities in Brazil to Europe. Officially, for now the airline just claims these planes will be used to “strengthen connectivity between South America and more distant destinations.”.

    Earlier this year, LATAM’s CEO did drop some hints that the plane could fly from Lima (LIM) and Brasilia (BSB) to the United States, and from Fortaleza (FOR) to Europe, though no final decisions have been announced.

    We can expect LATAM to offer an all-fresh passenger experience (by the carrier’s standards) onboard the Airbus A321XLRs. The airline plans to configure the planes with a total of 174 seats, including:.

    Sources indicate that throughout the plane, passengers can expect the Panasonic Astrova entertainment system, with over 2,300 hours of content, including 330 movies and 1,200 TV shows. Bluetooth audio will also be available at all seats, so that passengers can connect to their own headphones. The A321XLR will also be equipped with SES Wi-Fi, with LATAM Pass members getting complimentary browsing or messaging, depending on their membership tier and ticket type.

    According to recent reports, LATAM’s A321XLR business class will feature the Thompson Aero VantageSOLO product. So there will be 12 herringbone seats in a 1-1 configuration, with seats spread across six rows. This means all seats will have direct aisle access and doors. Business class seats will feature 19″ 4K OLED screens, AC power outlets, USB-C charging, and wireless charging.

    It also looks like the front row seats will be pretty special, as they’ll feature quite a bit of extra space, including a closet and wardrobe. It remains to be seen how the airline will monetize that extra space, if at all (maybe they’ll just be reserved for certain types of passengers?).

    Industry observers note that LATAM’s A321XLR business class will feature the Recaro R3 product. So there will be 162 seats in a 3-3 configuration, with six rows having extra legroom, and 21 rows having standard legroom. Economy class seats will feature 13″ 4K OLED screens, as well as USB-C outlets.

    The A321XLR is impressive for its range, and it’s understandable that the economics of such a small plane for long haul flying can be challenging. As a result, we’re really seeing airlines try to maximize capacity as much as possible, and this is also leading to so many airlines having very similar premium products on planes.

    LATAM will have herringbone seats on the A321XLR, just like… well, all current operators that use this primarily as a long haul aircraft, with the exception of Aer Lingus.

    For those keeping track at home, the Thompson Aero VantageSOLO product is what you’ll find in JetBlue’s Mint business class on select A321neo/LR aircraft, and it’s also what you’ll find in Iberia’s A321XLR business class.

    According to recent reports, while American’s A321XLR business class looks similar, it’s based on the Collins Aerospace Aurora seating platform, and that’s also what Air Canada has selected. Meanwhile United’s A321XLR business class also looks similar, but is based on the Elevate Altitude platform.

    Admittedly these planes all have better business class products than we found on long haul Boeing 757s years ago (the most direct replacement), and the tech is also greatly updated. That being noted, as a passenger experience geek, this sure is a boring plane… “you get a herringbone seat, you get a herringbone seat, you get a herringbone seat, everyone gets a herringbone seat!”.

    While not quite A321XLRs, credit to ITA Airways’ A321neo business class and Etihad’s A321LR business class for having reverse herringbone seats.

    To LATAM’s credit, I will say that the cabin finishes look gorgeous, so I hope they look as nice in real life as they do in renderings.

    Recent findings suggest that in early 2027, LATAM expects to start taking delivery of the Airbus A321XLR, which the airline looks to use to grow into newly introduced markets. The airline has now revealed what we can expect onboard these planes, and it includes herringbone seats with direct aisle access and doors in business class.

    According to recent reports, ultimately the cabin looks sleek, and it’s cool to see this in South America, where no other airline is currently offering such an experience. But still, it’s hard to get too excited when so many airlines are introducing a similar product.

    LATAM in general deserves credit for the extent to which it’s elevating the passenger experience in Latin America, as we’ve seen the airline introduce two new wide body business class products over the past several years.

    What do you make of LATAM’s upcoming A321XLR business class?

    Demand For $1,589 In Rental Car Damage Dropped After Pointing Out Illegal Fees

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, sixt demanded $1,589 from a customer for splatter and scuffs on a rental car, including nearly $500 in illegal fees.
    • Christopher Nienhuis, a Colorado resident, rented a Buick at Milwaukee airport in October while visiting Marquette University.
    • Sixt dropped the claim a week after being contacted by a news reporter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, sixt demanded $1,589 from a customer for splatter and scuffs on a rental car, including nearly $500 in illegal fees. The customer disputed the claim, complained to consumer agencies, and indicates it went to collections anyway. The bill disappeared once the practice came under scrutiny. Christopher Nienhuis, a Colorado resident, rented a Buick at Milwaukee airport in October while visiting Marquette University. Days after returning it, he received a damage bill for black splatter around the license plate and near the tires, along with white scuffing around the rear windshield. He says he didn’t cause the damage and that the black material could simply be washed off. Sixt dropped the claim a week after being contacted by a news reporter. Four Renters Were Billed Fees Wisconsin Doesn’t Allow Four customers with disputed claims from the same airport location complained of illegal charges. Todd Lofgren: $6,265 for “graffiti.” He described white specks near a tire and along the bumper. The photos and invoice were dated August 18, three days after he returned the car. The bill included $1,161 in prohibited fees. Sixt dropped it September 28 after he challenged it through multiple channels. Brenda Bassett: nearly $600 for a dent already documented. The rear dent was listed in her rental agreement before she took the 2025 Toyota. About $137 consisted of diminished value and appraisal fees. A September 15 letter came from Strala Group, which handles claims for Sixt. The claim was dropped. Autumn Wojciechowski: $872 for a scratch underneath the car. She’d photographed the vehicle before driving away, but not its underside. Nearly $200 of her October 2025 damage invoice consisted of prohibited fees. This claim was dropped, too. All four claims have been withdrawn. Wisconsin law limits damage liability to reasonable repair costs, reflecting discounts available to the rental company, or the vehicle’s value before the damage, whichever is lower. Loss of use, administrative charges and appraisal fees are prohibited. Diminished value charges (loss in resale value) aren’t allowed either. Sixt Already Settled A Damage Billing Lawsuit Sixt’s 2025 damage billing settlement addressed allegations involving estimated repairs, diminished value, loss of use and administrative charges. The $11 million package included about $2.87 million in potential refunds and $6.6 million in abandoned collection claims, along with legal and administrative costs. The incentives are lousy. A customer can pay to make a collection demand go away, turn it over to insurance, or spend hours fighting. If the company withdraws a bad claim only when someone gets enough attention, everyone else still has to decide whether contesting it is worth the trouble. I’ve called rental car fees the scammiest in travel. These damage add-ons are especially difficult to comparison shop because you don’t discover them until after you’ve returned the car. Sixt Isn’t Great, But You Expect Charges To Be Correct I’ve found Sixt offers an inferior experience in the U.S. market. My Miami rental years ago involved a Mercedes they didn’t and a proposed alternative of a $30 a day upgrade for a lesser car. I canceled and went to National. The Milwaukee airport remarked its lease requires Sixt to follow the law and allows termination for an uncured violation after notice. But the airport said it was waiting for the state consumer protection agency to determine that a violation occurred. It’s not yet clear whether they’ve stopped charging these fees in Wisconsin.     • The good news is that major ride-hailing players Uber, Lyft and Blacklane all have launched Thanksgiving offers, including one that is exclusive to our TPG members.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the busy Thanksgiving travel season is just about to kick off as millions take flight around the country. You can expect crowded terminals, long security lines and potentially surge-priced rides to and from the airport.

    The good news is that major ride-hailing players Uber, Lyft and Blacklane all have launched Thanksgiving offers, including one that is exclusive to our TPG members.

    Here's how to make the most of your holiday ride transport.

    Related: Here’s what Thanksgiving foods you can bring in your carry-on and what has to be checked.

    Recent findings suggest that through Nov. 30, Uber is running a promotion called "From Bad Seats to Better Rides." If you get squeezed into a middle seat with no armrest or end up in the last row by the lavatory, you could receive up to 30% off your Uber ride home from the airport.

    To take part, register your flight and seat details on Uber's Thanksgiving promotion page. Uber provides several examples of undesirable seats but has not published a complete list of what qualifies as undesirable. Individual savings vary, and terms apply, so check the offer added to your Uber account before booking. In our testing, you will not be required to submit a boarding pass or an image of your undesirable seat to receive a discount.

    It has been revealed that TPG tip: Link your Delta SkyMiles and Uber accounts and select Delta as your earning partner before you travel. You will earn 1 mile per eligible dollar on UberX airport rides, 2 miles per eligible dollar on Uber XL, Uber Comfort, Uber Black and Uber SUV rides and 3 miles per eligible dollar on Uber Reserve rides in the U.S. Note that taxes, fees, mandatory charges and tips do not earn miles.

    Related: From Starbucks to Uber: Airline and hotel partnerships that earn points and miles.

    Uber One Member Days run through Dec. 1, where Uber says members can unlock up to $500 in savings across rides, deliveries, hotels and other offers. Some deals are targeted, so check your email and your Uber app to see if you are eligible, but offers may include:.

    No purchase is necessary to enter either sweepstakes.

    Recent findings suggest that TPG tip: Link your Marriott Bonvoy and Uber accounts and select Marriott as your earning partner. You will earn 3 Marriott Bonvoy points per eligible dollar on Uber XL, Uber Comfort, Uber Black and Uber SUV rides in the U.S., including those booked with Reserve and 2 points per eligible dollar on UberX rides booked with Reserve. Members who have not linked the two accounts can also earn 1,000 bonus points for linking by Nov. 24, plus another 1,000 points after completing an eligible premium or Reserve ride by the same date.

    You can link both Delta and Marriott to Uber, but only one can be selected as the earning partner for a ride at a time, so choose which currency is more useful to you.

    Related: Marriott announces Uber partnership changes: The good, the bad and the totally worthless.

    United MileagePlus members can earn 8 United miles per eligible dollar on scheduled airport rides with Lyft through Nov. 30, twice the standard rate of 4 miles per dollar. Link your MileagePlus and Lyft accounts and select United as your active rewards partner before booking.

    According to recent reports, the offer applies to eligible rides requested, completed and paid for in the U.S. or Puerto Rico.

    Make sure you schedule your ride in advance, because unscheduled airport rides only earn 3 miles per eligible dollar, while most standard personal rides earn 1 mile per eligible dollar.

    Note that taxes, fees, tolls and tips do not earn miles.

    Sources indicate that TPG tip: Shift your rewards up a gear by paying with the (see rates and fees) or (see rates and fees), and you will earn 5 total Chase Ultimate Rewards points per dollar on qualifying Lyft purchases through Sept. 30, 2027. Both cards earn 1 point per dollar on purchases outside their bonus categories.

    In a recent development, sapphire Reserve cardholders also receive a $10 monthly in-app Lyft credit through Sept. 30, 2027. Unused credit expires at the end of each calendar month.

    Related: How to easily earn extra rewards on Lyft rides.

    If you would rather avoid a crowded airport pickup zone, why not treat yourself to Blacklane? The global luxury chauffeur service operates in more than 500 cities across more than 60 countries, and its fixed prices include standard taxes, tolls, tips and fees.

    According to recent reports, TPG members can right now receive an exclusive $80 credit toward two chauffeur journeys in the U.S. To claim it, sign in to or create a TPG account through the TPG Member Offers page, then click through to Blacklane from the offer.

    TPG tip: Bilt members can redeem Bilt Cash toward Blacklane rides each calendar year: up to $50 for Blue and Silver members, $100 for Gold members and $150 for Platinum members. Blacklane rides booked through Bilt also earn 1 Bilt Point per dollar.

    Related: No surge, no scramble: Why I loved using Blacklane for my latest airport transfer.

    Thanksgiving airport rides can be expensive, but this holiday season you may be able to reduce the cost and/or increase your rewards.

    Uber's bad-seat offer is the most straightforward discount if your aircraft seat qualifies and is a fun and lighthearted way to reward those whose seat allocation is unfortunate. Uber One members should also check their accounts for targeted airport and hotel offers, while the Lyft promotion is an easy way to earn double United miles on a ride many travelers will book anyway.

    Link your loyalty accounts, select the right earning partner and check your card benefits before traveling to ensure a happy and rewarding holiday.

    #42267. Tech Report: Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited Card Review: Is The $295 Fee Worth It?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2955 w)

    Tech Report: Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited Card Review: Is The $295 Fee Worth It?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card launched in March 2026.
    • Sources indicate that however, there are some things that could make this card worthwhile, including a potentially lucrative welcome offer, a solid return on spending, and some credits that can help offset the annual fee.
    • This post is my in-depth Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card launched in March 2026. On the surface, the card sounds rather uncompetitive — it has a $295 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers “just” 2% cash back on everyday spending, with limited bonus categories.

    Sources indicate that however, there are some things that could make this card worthwhile, including a potentially lucrative welcome offer, a solid return on spending, and some credits that can help offset the annual fee. If your business spends a lot, you value having an Amex, and you just want to earn simple cash back without a complex rewards structure, this could be a good option.

    This post is my in-depth Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review. Is the card worth it, and if so, under what circumstances? And what are the best alternatives?

    Link: Learn more about the Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card.

    Before I get into my Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review, let me briefly summarize the key details of the card:.

    Beyond that, here are what I consider to be some of the major pros and cons of the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited:.

    With the above out of the way, let’s look at the various aspects of the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited, from the welcome offer, to the fees, to the rewards structure, to the other perks. This card is fairly straightforward, so there’s not all that much to understand, for better or worse.

    It has been revealed that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited presently has a welcome offer where you can earn as high as $2,000 cash back after spending $50,000 within the first six months on eligible purchases. Reward Dollars can be redeemed as statement credits to offset transactions, or as a payment method for Amazon purchases.

    Given that the card ordinarily offers at least 2% cash back, that means spending $50,000 could earn you a minimum of $3,000 (if offered the full bonus amount), equivalent to 6% cash back on that amount of spending, which is solid.

    Admittedly the spending requirement is massive (it averages out to $8,333 per month over the course of six months), but I do think businesses that spend a lot might find this to be achievable. Furthermore, it’s nice that you have six months to complete the spending requirement, while many other cards give you only three months to reach the spending requirement.

    If you’re applying for the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited, be aware of Amex’s general restrictions on applying for cards, including the “once in a lifetime rule.” That means you’re not eligible for the welcome offer on the card if you’ve already had this card, though you are potentially eligible for the bonus if you’ve had other Amex cards.

    It has been revealed that anecdotally, I find Amex business cards to be quite easy to get approved for. I also love how with Amex, you can know if you’ll be approved with no credit score impact — the hard pull only happens after you’re told if you’re approved, and you accept the offer.

    Also keep in mind that if you’re concerned about staying under Chase’s 5/24 limit, applying for an Amex business card won’t count toward that, since it doesn’t show up on your personal credit report in that way.

    When it comes to credit score, there’s not a consistent credit score you need to get approved for the card, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility. Personally, I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has an annual fee of $295 (Rates & Fees), which is definitely on the steep side, especially given the relatively narrow appeal of the credits offered on the card, which require a lot of spending.

    With the card’s 2% cash back rewards structure, you’d essentially recoup the annual fee (in terms of rewards) after $14,750 in spending.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has an authorized user fee of $95 for the first 5 cards, and a $95 annual fee for each thereafter (Rates & Fees), though you can also get a no annual fee Employee Business Expense Card with no additional fee. Still, that’s a rather steep authorized user fee for a card that doesn’t actually offer many incremental perks. You can add up to 99 employee cards to your account.

    Sources indicate that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has no preset spending limit. The idea is that this gives you flexibility in ways that traditional credit cards don’t. The amount you can spend adapts based on factors such as your purchase, payment, and credit history. Rather than having a set limit, you could grow your purchasing power the more you consistently use your card and regularly make payments.

    Industry observers note that in fairness, it is also worth mentioning that not having a preset spending limit can also lead to some declines if the amount you can charge decreases, so it’s a little less predictable than a regular credit card. However, I find that more often than not, it works in the favor of cardmembers.

    Sources indicate that no Preset Spending Limit means your spending limit is flexible. Unlike a traditional card with a set limit, the amount you can spend adapts based on factors such as your purchase, payment, and credit history.

    In terms of its rewards structure, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers a minimum of unlimited 2% cash back on eligible purchases. On top of that, the card offers 5% cash back on flights and prepaid hotels booked through American Express Travel® Online. Just to do some very basic math:.

    According to recent reports, all cash back on the card is earned as Reward Dollars, which can be redeemed as statement credits to offset transactions, or as a payment method for Amazon purchases. Unfortunately there are no other redemption options, so you couldn’t directly deposit the cash back into a business checking account, or anything like tht.

    2% cash back on credit card spending is the “gold standard,” as I see it, so that’s excellent, and what everyone should be aiming for, at a minimum.

    Recent findings suggest that meanwhile the 5% cash back on Amex Travel might sound appealing, but there are some catches. If you can route travel spending that way, it’s a good option, but the catch is that you may sometimes find lower rates elsewhere, so there could be an opportunity cost to booking that way.

    According to recent reports, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers up to $2,400 in American Express One AP® statement credits, after spending $250,000 on eligible purchases on the card in a calendar year. Statement credits will be applied to the monthly bill charged to the card for Amex’s accounts payable solution, One AP, for the following calendar year, and this includes an auto-renewing platform access fee.

    American Express One AP® is an accounts payable solution that can help transform the way your business pays suppliers. With One AP, you can streamline your supplier invoice payments on a single platform and pay by virtual card, check, and ACH. Enrollment is required.

    In a recent development, this program charges a $200 monthly fee to pay vendors with non-cards, plus has a fee for checks and ACHs over a certain limit. So the $2,400 annual credit can potentially fully cover your monthly fee. While this is potentially a nice feature, keep in mind that many platforms already offer this as a built in feature at no extra cost, so it’s not really that special.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers the Pay Over Time feature, whereby cardmembers can carry a balance with interest on eligible charges, up to the Pay Over Time limit. The way this works, eligible charges will automatically be added to a Pay Over Time balance, up to the Pay Over Time limit.

    In a recent development, you can choose to pay for these charges over time with interest, or you can pay your full balance each month, whichever is best for your business. You must pay in full any charge or a portion of a charge that is not added to a Pay Over Time balance.

    Sources indicate that personally, I recommend paying the balance in full each billing cycle if possible, to avoid interest charges, especially given how high they can be. However, I think it’s worth clarifying that the Pay Over Time option is possible, given that this isn’t a traditional credit card.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s also worth emphasizing the difference between the Pay Over Time and the Pay In Full Limit. The latter could be an amount that has to be paid in full, and there’s no option to pay that over time with interest charges.

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card earns 2% cash back, and I consider that to be the minimum “gold standard” of credit card rewards. So the card’s rewards structure is perfectly fine. The 5% cash back on travel is also pretty limiting, given that you have to book through Amex.

    Sources indicate that I think the issue is the steep annual fee, given that there are also much more affordable (and even no annual fee) cards with that kind of a rewards structure. In fairness, Amex doesn’t have another business card earning unlimited 2% cash back, so this is at least a latest product for the card issuer. It’s just not a new concept more broadly, and there are lots of competing cards that I’d consider to be superior.

    So who should consider the card? As I see it, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is targeted at a specific demographic. This card could make sense for the following types of customers:.

    I do truly think this is a niche product. But the idea is that if you’re a small business owner charging hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars on credit cards per year, that annual fee won’t make much of a difference.

    Still, I’d like to compare this to some other popular products, as I think there are other cards that may be a better fit for some other people.

    Perhaps the best direct comparison to the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card (learn more). The card has no annual fee (Rates & Fees) and offers 2% cash back on the first $50,000 spent every calendar year (and 1% cash back thereafter).

    According to recent reports, the upside here is obvious, as you’re earning 2% cash back with no fee. The downside is that the welcome offer is much smaller (though also with a smaller spending requirement), the card has foreign transaction fees, you’re capped at earning 2% cash back on the first $50,000 spent annually, and the card does have a preset spending limit.

    For a small business mostly spending money domestically, the Amex Blue Business Cash is a great alternative to the Amex Graphite Business Cash.

    Another potential alternative to the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is The Blue Business® Plus Credit Card from American Express (learn more). The card has no annual fee (Rates & Fees) and offers 2x Membership Rewards points on the first $50,000 spent every calendar year (and 1x points thereafter).

    Industry observers note that if you’re good at redeeming points, that’s a pretty incredible return, since based on my latest miles & points valuations, Amex points are worth 1.7 cents each, for a return of up to 3.4%. The downsides to the Amex Blue Business Plus are otherwise identical to those on the Amex Blue Business Cash — the welcome offer is much smaller (though also with a smaller spending requirement), the card has foreign transaction fees, you’re capped at earning 2x points on the first $50,000 spent annually, and the card does have a preset spending limit.

    So the card is either useful if $50,000 covers your annual business spending, or you’re willing to use another card after you hit that initial $50,000 spending cap.

    Speaking of premium Amex business cards, it’s also worth comparing the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the American Express® Business Gold Card (learn more). The Amex Business Gold has a $375 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers an incredible rewards structure (with up to 4x Membership Rewards points in select categories), plus statement credits that can greatly help offset the annual fee.

    As I see it, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is the better option if you value cash back and a straightforward rewards structure, while the Amex Business Gold is the better option if you can take advantage of the bonus categories, and are willing to put in the effort to maximize points.

    While the above comparisons are all to Amex cards, I think it’s also worth comparing the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the Capital One Spark Cash Plus (learn more), as it’s perhaps the most direct competitor.

    The card has a massive welcome offer of $2,000 cash back after spending $30,000 within the first three months (plus an additional $2,000 cash back bonus for every $500,000 spent during the first year), offers 5% cash back on select Capital One Business Travel purchases and 2% cash back with no caps and no foreign transaction fees on other purchases, and it has a $150 annual fee. Furthermore, the card offers an annual bonus of $150 if you spend at least $150,000 on the card in a calendar year, essentially rebating the annual fee.

    I do think the Capital One Spark Cash Plus is more compelling than the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card on balance, unless you specifically have a reason you’d like an Amex, or value the statement credits tied to spending $250,000 per year.

    I’d also like to compare the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the Ink Business Premier® Credit Card (learn more), as it’s another potentially lucrative cash back card.

    It has been revealed that in addition to a massive welcome offer of $1,000 cash back after spending $10,000 within the first three months, the card offers 5% cash back on Chase Travel purchases, 2.5% cash back on purchases of $5,000 or more, and 2% cash back on all other purchases, with no foreign transaction fees, and it has a $195 annual fee. So if you have a business that frequently makes large purchases, the Chase Ink Business Premier could be a great alternative.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Card has a $295 annual fee, and offers unlimited 2% cash back, with no preset spending limit, plus a large welcome offer. The card also offers up to $2,400 in American Express One AP® statement credits, after spending $250,000 on eligible purchases on the card in a calendar year.

    In a recent development, ultimately I’d consider this to be a niche card. The card could be worth getting for the excellent welcome offer, and it could be worth it if you have a business that spends a huge amount, and values the lack of a preset spending limit, the card’s Amex branding, and/or the statement credits.

    Beyond that, though, I tend to think there are better options. If you’re not a huge spender, the Amex Blue Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Plus are excellent options. If you’re willing to maximize points and bonus categories, consider the Amex Business Gold. And if you’re looking for the best direct alternative that’s arguably more lucrative, consider the Capital One Spark Cash Plus.

    If you want to learn more about the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card, follow this link.

    Industry observers note that the following links will direct you to the rates and fees for mentioned American Express Cards. These include: American Express® Business Gold Card (Rates & Fees), The Blue Business® Plus Credit Card from American Express (Rates & Fees), The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card (Rates & Fees), and Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card (Rates & Fees).
